definition_zh: 人类学研究；以田野与比较方法对某一人类社会或文化所作的专题研究
definition_en: a research project or published account that examines a human society or culture by anthropological methods
core_image: 一间借住的屋子、一叠按日期编号的笔记、一张把几个社会并排画出的比较表
scene: 书架最上层放着一叠关于同一座村庄的报告，年份不同，封面却几乎一样。Her anthropological study of the village began with a question about names.
sceneCN: 这里「人类学研究」指一项以田野与比较为方法的专题研究（第 1 个义项：作为研究项目）；句意为她对这座村庄的人类学研究始于一个关于姓名的问题。

pos.zh: 人类学研究（可数，指一项研究或一份成果；复数 anthropological studies）

collocations.zh: 一项经典的人类学研究
关于亲属关系的人类学研究
关于仪式的人类学研究

derivatives.zh: anthropo-（希腊「人」）+ -logy（希腊「学问」）→ 人类学：这项研究所属的学科
拉丁 studium「热忱、钻研」经古法语 estudie → 研究；学习（语义偏移：从「热心」到「用心的成果」）
拉丁 studere「用心」的现在分词名词化 → 学生（语义偏移：正在用心的人）
studium + -ous（充满）→ 好学的（语义偏移：以用心为特征）
ethno-（希腊 ethnos「族群」）+ -graphy（希腊「书写」）→ 民族志：这类研究的典型成品

senses.title: A research project
senses.titleCN: 作为研究项目：有计划地追问一个问题
senses.definition: a planned inquiry into one society or culture, with a question and a design
senses.definitionCN: 针对某一社会或文化、带着问题与设计的有计划考察
senses.example: Her anthropological study of the village began with a question about names.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这座村庄的人类学研究始于一个关于姓名的问题。
senses.why: Study came from Latin studium, 'eager application', so the phrase names an application of the mind to a case; anthropological says which instruments the application uses.
senses.whyCN: study 出自拉丁 studium「热忱、钻研」，因此这个短语指心智对某个案例的用心；anthropological 则说明用的是哪套仪器。

senses.title: The published account
senses.titleCN: 作为成果：写成书或论文的那一份
senses.definition: the book or article in which the inquiry is finally set out
senses.definitionCN: 研究最终写成的书或论文
senses.example: The anthropological study appeared eight years after the last field visit.
senses.exampleCN: 这项人类学研究在最后一次田野访问八年之后出版。
senses.why: In academic English a study often means the document rather than the doing: what is cited in a footnote is the printed result, not the years behind it.
senses.whyCN: 在学术英语里，study 常指文献而非活动：脚注里引用的是印出来的结果，而不是它背后的那些年。

senses.title: The fieldwork itself
senses.titleCN: 作为田野活动：住在当地做观察的过程
senses.definition: the activity of living among people and observing their daily life
senses.definitionCN: 住在当地人中间观察其日常生活的活动
senses.example: The anthropological study required two years of learning the local verb forms.
senses.exampleCN: 这项人类学研究需要两年时间去学当地的动词形式。
senses.why: Residence is the discipline's instrument, and study can name the instrument's use: the long stay is the study, before anything is written.
senses.whyCN: 驻留是这门学科的仪器，study 可以指仪器的使用：在写成文字之前，那段长住就是研究。

senses.title: A comparative investigation
senses.titleCN: 作为比较：把多个案例并排放
senses.definition: an inquiry that sets several cases side by side in order to compare them
senses.definitionCN: 把若干案例并置以便比较的考察
senses.example: Their anthropological study compared burial customs in four river valleys.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的人类学研究比较了四条河谷的丧葬习俗。
senses.why: Comparison is what turns a description into anthropology; a single case can be described, but a study in this sense needs at least two.
senses.whyCN: 比较才把描述变成人类学；单一案例可以被描述，但此义上的研究至少需要两个案例。

senses.title: A long-term community study
senses.titleCN: 作为长期跟踪：隔年回访同一社区
senses.definition: a repeated inquiry into one community over many years or decades
senses.definitionCN: 在多年乃至数十年间反复回访同一社区的考察
senses.example: The anthropological study returned to the same households in three different decades.
senses.exampleCN: 这项人类学研究在三个不同年代回访了同一批家庭。
senses.why: Because social life changes slowly and unevenly, only repetition over time can show what is stable and what is passing; the phrase then denotes a series rather than one visit.
senses.whyCN: 社会生活变得缓慢而不均匀，只有跨时间的重复才能显出什么稳定、什么短暂；此时短语指一个系列，而非一次访问。

senses.title: A method-defined study
senses.titleCN: 按方法界定：以参与观察为核心的研究
senses.definition: a study defined by participant observation rather than by survey or experiment
senses.definitionCN: 以参与观察、而非问卷或实验来界定的研究
senses.example: The anthropological study was judged by its method, not only by its findings.
senses.exampleCN: 这项人类学研究是按其方法、而不只按结论来评判的。
senses.why: The adjective can attach to the method rather than the field: work is anthropological when it was done by living there, whatever its subject.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词可以附在方法上而非学科上：只要靠住在那里完成，不论题目是什么，工作就是人类学的。

senses.title: A branch-specific study
senses.titleCN: 属于某一分支：如生物人类学的研究
senses.definition: an inquiry located in one branch, such as biological or linguistic work
senses.definitionCN: 位于生物、语言等某一分支之内的考察
senses.example: A biological anthropological study measured growth in the same children each year.
senses.exampleCN: 一项生物人类学研究每年测量同一批儿童的生长。
senses.why: Once the four fields split, the phrase needed qualifying adjectives; the branch name tells you which instruments were used and which evidence counts.
senses.whyCN: 四分支分开之后，这个短语需要限定形容词；分支名告诉你用了哪些仪器、哪种证据才算数。

senses.title: A commissioned study
senses.titleCN: 受委托的研究：为机构解决具体问题
senses.definition: a study paid for by an institution to answer a practical question
senses.definitionCN: 由机构出资、为回答实际问题而做的研究
senses.example: The ministry commissioned an anthropological study of why the clinic went unused.
senses.exampleCN: 该部门委托做一项人类学研究，追问诊所为何无人使用。
senses.why: Study can be bought: a client pays for a question and a report, and the same methods serve a decision rather than a discipline.
senses.whyCN: 研究可以被购买：委托方付钱买一个问题与一份报告，同样的方法服务于决策，而非学科。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek-derived field adjective to a Latin-derived noun for eager application; the noun's history is plain, the Greek stem's is not.
intro.cn: 这个短语把希腊来源的学科形容词接在拉丁来源的「用心」名词上；名词的历史清楚，希腊词干则不然。

items.en: Anthropos 'human being' is well attested, but its internal analysis is disputed; the reading as aner 'man' plus ops 'face' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: anthropos「人」书证充分，但内部构造有争议；读作 anēr「男人」加 ōps「脸」只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: -Logia 'account, study' derives from logos 'word, reason' and legein 'to gather, say'; the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
items.cn: -logia「叙述、学问」出自 logos「言词、理性」与 legein「收集、说出」；更深的印欧词根为重构。

items.en: Studium meant 'eagerness, application, pursuit of knowledge', from studere 'to be eager for'. The verb's origin is not settled beyond Latin, and any earlier form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: studium 意为「热忱、用心、求知的 pursuit」，来自 studere「热衷于」。该动词在拉丁语之前来源未定，更早的形式均为重构。

items.en: Old French estudie carried the noun into English in the thirteenth century, first as the state of being eager, then as the object pursued.
items.cn: 古法语 estudie 在 13 世纪把这个名词带入英语，先指用心的状态，后指所钻研的对象。

items.en: The combination with anthropological is a nineteenth-century product: the field needed a countable noun for one piece of work, and study supplied it.
items.cn: 与 anthropological 的组合是 19 世纪的产物：这门学科需要一个可数的名词来指一件具体工作，study 正好补上。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact phrase has no fixed first citation, the make-up of anthropos is unsettled, and the pre-Latin origin of studere is unknown.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这一确切短语没有公认的最早书证；anthropos 的构造无定论；studere 在拉丁语之前的来源不明。

note.en: Group one holds near-identical phrases and words that are routinely substituted; group two holds the kinds of writing a study turns into.
note.cn: 第一组是常被直接替换的近形短语与单词；第二组是研究会变成的几种文字成品。

entries.definition: The activity of collecting data among people; a study is what that activity eventually makes.
entries.definitionCN: 在人群中收集资料的活动；研究是这项活动最终做出的东西。

entries.definition: The written description of one people, often the form an anthropological study takes.
entries.definitionCN: 对单一族群的文字描述，常是人类学研究所采取的形式。

entries.definition: An intensive inquiry into a single instance; it needs no fieldwork and belongs to no particular discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 对单一实例的深入考察；不必田野，也不专属某一学科。

entries.definition: A study that asks fixed questions of many people at once, rather than living among a few.
entries.definitionCN: 一次向许多人提出固定问题的研究，而非住在少数人中间。

entries.definition: A book-length treatment of one subject; the usual final shape of a long study.
entries.definitionCN: 对单一主题的整书篇幅处理；长期研究的常见最终形态。

entries.definition: A short published report of findings, narrower and faster than a monograph.
entries.definitionCN: 较短的研究成果发表形式，比专著更窄更快。

entries.definition: A formal account prepared for an institution, often the product of a commissioned study.
entries.definitionCN: 为机构准备的正式陈述，常是受委托研究的成品。

entries.definition: The long research text that earns a doctorate, usually the first big study a practitioner completes.
entries.definitionCN: 为取得博士学位而写的长篇研究文本，通常是从业者完成的第一项大研究。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real genre names and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实文体名与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: anthropos 'human' + logia 'study' + studium 'eager application': an eager application of the discipline to one case.
normal.cn: anthropos「人」+ logia「学问」+ studium「用心」：把学问用心地施于一个案例。

normal.en: A study is first a doing, then a document; the phrase can mean either, which is why citations sound like objects.
normal.cn: 研究先是活动，后是文献；短语两义兼有，所以引文里听起来像物件。

normal.en: The family runs study, student, studious, anthropology, anthropological, ethnography.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 study、student、studious、anthropology、anthropological、ethnography。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: conduct a study, publish a study, a long-term study.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：开展研究、发表研究、长期研究。

normal.en: Shape check: question, design, residence, notes, comparison, account.
normal.cn: 结构检查：问题、设计、驻留、笔记、比较、成文。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf where ten reports about one village stand in a row like years on a ruler.
abstract.cn: 想象书架上一排关于同一村庄的报告，像尺子上的年份。

abstract.en: Picture a notebook that grows heavier than the suitcase it travelled in.
abstract.cn: 想象一本笔记比它随行的箱子还重。

abstract.en: Picture a footnote pointing to a book that took longer to write than the building it is stored in.
abstract.cn: 想象一条脚注指向一本书，写它花的时间比存放它的楼还久。

examples.en: The anthropological study was rejected by two journals before it changed the field.
examples.cn: 这项人类学研究被两家期刊拒绝，后来却改变了这个领域。

examples.en: Students read an anthropological study of a market and then visit one.
examples.cn: 学生先读一份关于市场的人类学研究，再去逛一个市场。

examples.en: A good anthropological study says how the researcher changed the place being studied.
examples.cn: 好的人类学研究会说清研究者如何改变了被研究的地方。

dict_mnemonic.text: anthropo（人）+ logical（学问的）+ study（研究）＝ 用人类学方法做的一项研究；记「先住进去，再并排比较，最后成书」。

root: 希腊 anthrōpos「人」+ -logia「学问」构成学科形容词；拉丁 studium「热忱、钻研」（来自 studere）经古法语 estudie 构成 study。anthropos 与 studere 的更深来源均不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one piece of work from question to print: the project, the book, the residence, the comparison, the decades of return visits, the method that defines it, the branch it belongs to and the client who paid for it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一件工作从提问走到付印：项目、成书、驻留、比较、数十年的回访、界定它的方法、它所属的分支，以及出钱的委托方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a borrowed room, a numbered notebook and a comparison table of several societies on one page.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间借住的屋子、一叠编号的笔记，以及一页并排画出几个社会的比较表。

branches.en: BEFORE AND AFTER PRINT: the planned inquiry, then the document that outlives it.
branches.cn: 付印前后：先是计划中的考察，后是比它活得更久的文献。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT AND ITS RULE: living there, and the method that makes living there count as evidence.
branches.cn: 仪器与其规则：住在那里，以及使这段居住成为证据的方法。

branches.en: TWO AXES OF COMPARISON: several cases side by side, and one case followed across decades.
branches.cn: 比较的两轴：多个案例并排，以及一个案例跨越数十年。

branches.en: THE BRANCH LABEL: the qualifying adjective decides which instruments and which evidence.
branches.cn: 分支标签：限定形容词决定用哪些仪器、认哪种证据。

branches.en: THE CLIENT: a paid question turns the same method toward a decision.
branches.cn: 委托方：付费的问题把同一套方法转向一个决策。

intro.en: The phrase is a Greek compound adjective plus a Latin noun, so two different morphological systems meet in one term.
intro.cn: 这个短语是希腊复合形容词加拉丁名词，两套构词系统在一个术语里相遇。

latinIntro.en: Greek anthropos and -logia build the adjective; Latin studium builds the noun, and the Latin noun family is the one that grew in English.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 anthropos 与 -logia 构成形容词；拉丁 studium 构成名词，而英语中长大的是拉丁名词词族。

items.example: The anthropo- element also builds anthropoid.
items.exampleCN: anthropo- 也构成 anthropoid。

items.example: The suffix is shared with biology.
items.exampleCN: 该后缀与 biology 共用。

items.example: The ending makes a relational adjective from the field name.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾把学科名变成关系形容词。

items.example: The Latin noun names the mental effort behind the work.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词指工作背后的心力。

items.meaning: a piece of research; to inquire
items.example: The noun and the verb share one Latin source.
items.exampleCN: 名词与动词共享同一个拉丁来源。

items.meaning: one who applies himself to learning
items.example: The ending marks the person in the act of applying.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾标记正处于用功状态的人。

items.example: The adjective describes the habit, not the project.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述习惯，而非项目。

items.example: Ethnography is the genre a study often becomes.
items.exampleCN: 民族志常是研究最终变成的文体。

items.example: The adjective limits which methods count.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词限定哪些方法算数。

latinEntries.structure: anthropologia, -ae (New Latin, f., first declension, from Greek)

latinEntries.meaning: to be eager for, apply oneself

definition_zh: 人；人类的；有人情味的；具有常人之局限的
definition_en: a person, or something belonging to, made by, or characteristic of people
core_image: 火山灰里的一枚脚印：不是骨骼，却比骨骼更能说明有人曾在这里走过
scene: 新出土的足印压在火山灰里，围观的人忽然都安静了。A human footprint in the ash was the first proof that anyone had walked here.
sceneCN: 这里「人的」指属于人的、由人留下的（第 2 个义项：属于人类的）；句意为火山灰里的一枚人的脚印，是曾有人在此行走的第一份证据。

pos.zh: 人；人类（可数，复数 humans，多用于科学或对比语境）
人的；人类的；有人情味的；常人的（带局限意味）

derivatives.zh: human + -ity（性质名词后缀）→ 人性；人类（语义偏移：从个体属性到集体总称）
human + -ly（副词后缀）→ 以人的方式；在人力所及的范围内
in-（否定）+ human → 非人的；残忍的（语义偏移：不像人会做的事）
super-（超过）+ human → 超人的（语义偏移：超出常人的能力）
human + -ize（使成为）→ 使人性化；使变得可亲
de-（去除）+ humanize → 使失去人性（语义偏移：剥夺人的尊严）
humanity + -arian（信奉者）→ 人道主义的；人道主义者
human + -oid（形似）→ 类人的；人形机器

senses.title: A person
senses.titleCN: 人：一个属于人类的个体
senses.definition: a member of the species Homo sapiens, considered as an individual
senses.definitionCN: 智人物种的一个成员，作为个体来看
senses.example: A human footprint in the ash was the first proof that anyone had walked here.
senses.exampleCN: 火山灰里的一枚人的脚印，是曾有人在此行走的第一份证据。
senses.why: Human entered English as an adjective from Latin humanus, and only later became a countable noun; the noun keeps the adjective's sense of 'belonging to people'.
senses.whyCN: human 先以形容词身份从拉丁 humanus 进入英语，后来才作可数名词；名词仍保留形容词「属于人的」之意。

senses.title: Belonging to people
senses.titleCN: 属于人类的：人的身体、遗骸与痕迹
senses.definition: of, belonging to, or produced by people
senses.definitionCN: 属于人、由人产生或与人有关的
senses.example: The trench cut through a layer of human bones and broken pots.
senses.exampleCN: 探沟切过一层人骨与碎陶。
senses.why: Humanus was the adjective of homo 'person', so the plainest sense simply marks whose body, whose trace, whose business it is.
senses.whyCN: humanus 是 homo「人」的形容词，因此最朴素的义项只是标明这是谁的身体、谁的痕迹、谁的事情。

senses.title: Kind, compassionate
senses.titleCN: 有人情味的：待人以宽厚
senses.definition: showing the warmth and mercy expected of people toward one another
senses.definitionCN: 待人有如人应有的温厚与怜悯
senses.example: The guard made a human gesture and let the family wait inside.
senses.exampleCN: 看守做了一个有人情味的举动，让这家人在屋里等。
senses.why: Latin humanus already meant 'kind, courteous' as well as 'of a person'; English split the two senses later, but the older warmth survives in phrases like a human touch.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 humanus 除「属于人」外本就含「仁厚、有礼」；英语后来把两义分开，但那份温度仍留在「有人情味的举动」这类说法里。

senses.title: Characteristic of people, with limits
senses.titleCN: 常人的：带着人的局限与易错
senses.definition: showing the weaknesses that people are known for, such as error or fatigue
senses.definitionCN: 显出人常有的弱点，如失误与疲惫
senses.example: The report blamed human error rather than the machine.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把责任归于人为失误，而非机器。
senses.why: If the adjective marks what belongs to people, it also marks what people cannot avoid; the same word that praises warmth can excuse a mistake.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个形容词标记属于人的东西，它也标记人无法避免的东西；同一个词既称赞温厚，也替失误开脱。

senses.title: Mortal, not divine
senses.titleCN: 会死的：不是神，终有一死
senses.definition: subject to death and limitation, as opposed to divine or immortal
senses.definitionCN: 会死、有限，与神或不朽相对
senses.example: Every human claim to certainty eventually meets a counterexample.
senses.exampleCN: 人对确定性的每一份主张，最终都会遇到反例。
senses.why: The oldest contrast in the word's family is homo against deus: to call something human is to place it on the mortal side of that line.
senses.whyCN: 这个词族里最古老的对照是 homo 对 deus：把某物称为 human，就是把它放在那条线的会死的一侧。

senses.title: Designed for people
senses.titleCN: 为人设计的：便于人使用或阅读
senses.definition: made to be used or understood easily by people rather than by machines
senses.definitionCN: 为便于人使用或理解而设计，而非为机器
senses.example: The manual was rewritten in human language after the first version failed.
senses.exampleCN: 第一版失败后，手册被改写成人的语言。
senses.why: In computing the adjective marks the user's side of an interface: human-readable, human-in-the-loop, where the machine is the other party.
senses.whyCN: 在计算机领域，这个形容词标记接口属于使用者的一侧：「便于人阅读」「人在回路中」这类说法里，机器则是另一方。

senses.title: Caused by people
senses.titleCN: 由人造成的：人为的而非自然的
senses.definition: caused by people rather than by natural processes
senses.definitionCN: 由人而非自然过程造成的
senses.example: The cliff is retreating faster because of human removal of sand.
senses.exampleCN: 由于人为挖沙，这段崖壁后退得更快。
senses.why: Once human means 'belonging to people', it can also mean 'traceable to people as a cause', which is how it became the standard label in environmental writing.
senses.whyCN: 既然 human 意为「属于人的」，它也可指「可追溯到人这个原因」，于是成了环境写作里的标准标签。

senses.title: The species in scientific use
senses.titleCN: 作为物种：科学语境中的整体称谓
senses.definition: the species taken as a whole in scientific or statistical statements
senses.definitionCN: 在科学或统计陈述中被当作整体的物种
senses.example: The human genome was read out faster than anyone predicted.
senses.exampleCN: 人类基因组被读出的速度超过任何人的预料。
senses.why: Science needs a mass noun for the species, and the adjective supplied one: the human genome, human populations, human evolution.
senses.whyCN: 科学需要一个指称整个物种的物质名词，形容词正好补上：人类基因组、人类种群、人类演化。

senses.title: What it is to be human
senses.titleCN: 人的处境：作为人意味着什么
senses.definition: the condition of being a person, with its awareness of death and choice
senses.definitionCN: 作为人而存在的处境，包括对死亡与选择的自觉
senses.example: The novel is less about events than about what makes a life human.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说与其说写事件，不如说写是什么让一段生活成为人的生活。
senses.why: The adjective's oldest layer still supports an existential question: human can name not a property but the whole condition of being a person.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词最古老的一层仍支撑一个存在论问题：human 可以不是指某项属性，而是指作为人的整个处境。

intro.en: Human came straight from Latin humanus; the family is clear, but the origin of the Latin noun homo behind it is one of the standing uncertainties of Indo-European etymology.
intro.cn: human 直接来自拉丁 humanus；词族清楚，但其后的拉丁名词 homo 的来源是印欧词源学里长期未决的问题之一。

items.en: Homo, hominis meant 'human being, person, man'. Some scholars connect it with humus 'earth, ground', giving 'earthling'; that reading is a hypothesis, and the forms proposed for a shared Indo-European source are reconstructions.
items.cn: homo, hominis 意为「人、个体、男人」。有学者把它与 humus「土地」联系起来，得出「地上之人」；这一读法是假说，为共同印欧来源拟出的形式均为重构。

items.en: Humanus 'human, humane, kind' was the adjective of homo, and it covered both 'of a person' and 'good to a person'.
items.cn: humanus「人的、仁厚的」是 homo 的形容词，兼含「属于人」与「善待人的」。

items.en: Old French hume, humain carried both the noun and the adjective into French; the adjective reached English through it in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 古法语 hume、humain 把名词与形容词带入法语；形容词经它在中世纪进入英语。

items.en: English borrowed the same Latin adjective twice: humane came earlier through French for the kind sense, and human was borrowed later from Latin for the neutral sense, so the two spellings now divide the work.
items.cn: 英语两次借入同一个拉丁形容词：humane 较早经法语而来，承担「仁厚」义；human 较晚直接从拉丁语借入，承担中性义，如今两种拼写分工。

items.en: From the seventeenth century human widened into science and law, giving fixed phrases such as human body, human rights and human error.
items.cn: 自 17 世纪起，human 扩展到科学与法律，形成人体、人权、人为失误等固定搭配。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the link between homo and humus is unproven, and no pre-Latin form for either is attested, so all such forms are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：homo 与 humus 的联系未获证明，二者在拉丁语之前的形式均无书证，因此这类形式全属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the doublet and compounds that are constantly confused with human; group two holds words for a person or for people as a whole.
note.cn: 第一组是常与 human 混淆的同源双式词与复合词；第二组是指个体或全体人的词。

entries.tag: the kind half of the doublet
entries.definition: The same Latin adjective borrowed earlier through French: it means compassionate and merciful, and is used of treatment, never of species.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个拉丁形容词较早经法语借入：意为仁慈、宽厚，用于对待方式，从不用于物种。

entries.definition: The collective name for people, or the quality of being kind; the adjective's abstract counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 人的集体称谓，或仁厚的品质；是该形容词的抽象对应词。

entries.definition: Not human, or lacking what people ought to feel; it denies both the species sense and the kind sense.
entries.definitionCN: 非人的，或缺乏人应有的情感；同时否定物种义与仁厚义。

entries.definition: Built with -oid 'resembling': having a human form, said of robots and fictional beings.
entries.definitionCN: 以 -oid「形似」构成：具有人的外形，用于机器人与虚构生物。

entries.definition: An individual regarded as having rights and a self; human is the biological and adjectival word.
entries.definitionCN: 被视为拥有权利与自我的个体；human 是生物性与形容词性的说法。

entries.definition: A single member of a group, stressing separateness rather than species.
entries.definitionCN: 群体中的单一成员，强调单独而非物种。

entries.definition: The traditional collective noun for people, now often replaced by humankind because of its masculine form.
entries.definitionCN: 指全体人的传统集体名词，因其阳性形式，现常被 humankind 取代。

entries.definition: A being that must die; it stresses the contrast with gods rather than membership in a species.
entries.definitionCN: 必死的存在；强调与神的对照，而非物种归属。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real doublets and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实同源双式词与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin homo gives the noun, humanus gives the adjective, and English borrowed the adjective twice as human and humane.
normal.cn: 拉丁 homo 提供名词，humanus 提供形容词，英语把形容词借了两次，成为 human 与 humane。

normal.en: The family runs human, humane, humanity, inhuman, superhuman, humanize, dehumanize, humanitarian, humanoid.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 human、humane、humanity、inhuman、superhuman、humanize、dehumanize、humanitarian、humanoid。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: human rights, human body, human error, human remains.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：人权、人体、人为失误、人类遗骸。

normal.en: The computing sense lives in human-readable and human-in-the-loop.
normal.cn: 计算机义活在「便于人阅读」与「人在回路中」这类说法里。

normal.en: humus 'earth' is only a hypothesis behind homo, so do not build a memory on 'earthling' alone.
normal.cn: humus「土地」只是 homo 背后的假说，别把记忆全建在「地上之人」上。

abstract.en: Picture a footprint that outlasts the foot by a hundred thousand years.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚脚印比那只脚多活十几万年。

abstract.en: Picture a guard who breaks one rule and thereby proves he is a person.
abstract.cn: 想象一名看守破了一次规矩，反而证明他是个人。

abstract.en: Picture a form designed so that no machine could ever enjoy filling it in.
abstract.cn: 想象一张表被设计得任何机器都不会乐意填。

examples.en: Human remains at the site were dated to the same century as the pottery.
examples.cn: 遗址中的人类遗骸与那些陶器被定到同一世纪。

examples.en: The system failed for human reasons: nobody had written down the handover.
examples.cn: 系统因人的原因失效：没有人把交接写下来。

examples.en: She argued that reading is a human activity before it is a technical one.
examples.cn: 她主张阅读先是人的活动，其次才是技术活动。

dict_mnemonic.text: human（人的）来自拉丁 homo（人）+ -anus（形容词词尾）；记「一个词三张脸：物种、仁厚、易错」。

root: 拉丁 humanus「人的、仁厚的」，来自 homo「人」+ -anus（形容词词尾）；homo 更深来源不确定，与 humus「土地」的联系、以及「地上之人」的读法均为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses spread from a single Latin adjective: one person, what belongs to people, warmth toward people, the limits of people, mortality, design for users, human causation, the species as a whole, and the condition of being a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从同一个拉丁形容词展开：一个人、属于人的东西、对人的温厚、人的局限、必死性、为用户而设计、人的成因、作为整体的物种，以及作为人的处境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a footprint in volcanic ash, more eloquent than any bone about who once walked there.
core.cn: 核心意象：火山灰里的一枚脚印，比任何骨骼都更能说明谁曾在那里走过。

branches.en: ONE AND MANY: an individual, then whatever belongs to such individuals.
branches.cn: 一与多：先是个体，再是属于这类个体的一切。

branches.en: THE SAME WORD BOTH WAYS: the warmth people ought to show, and the error they cannot avoid.
branches.cn: 同一个词的两面：人应有的温厚，与人无法避免的失误。

branches.en: THE CONDITION: mortality on one side, the whole question of what a life is on the other.
branches.cn: 处境：一边是会死，另一边是一段生活究竟是什么。

branches.en: MADE BY AND FOR PEOPLE: an interface built for users, a cliff cut by their shovels.
branches.cn: 为人所造、由人所为：为使用者建的界面，被人的铲子削去的崖壁。

branches.en: THE SPECIES AS AN OBJECT: science needs a mass noun, and the adjective supplies it.
branches.cn: 作为对象的物种：科学需要物质名词，形容词正好补上。

intro.en: Human is a Latin adjective whose stem also builds a large English family, with two borrowings of the same word and several productive prefixes.
intro.cn: human 是一个拉丁形容词，其词干在英语里长成一大族，同一个词被借两次，还接上若干能产前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin homo supplies the stem homin-; humanus supplies the adjective; the same adjective entered English twice, as humane and human. The family also includes post-Latin formations on human- alone.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 homo 提供词干 homin-；humanus 提供形容词；同一形容词两次进入英语，成为 humane 与 human。词族也包含只在 human- 上构成的后拉丁词。

items.example: The stem appears in hominid and hominin.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干出现在 hominid 与 hominin 中。

items.example: The ending turned the noun for a person into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把指人的名词变成形容词。

items.structure: humanus through Old French humain and direct Latin borrowing
items.example: Human is both the adjective and the countable noun.
items.exampleCN: human 既是形容词，也是可数名词。

items.structure: humanus through Old French, borrowed earlier
items.example: Humane treatment is the older French-shaped borrowing.
items.exampleCN: humane 是较早的法国形状借词。

items.meaning: the quality of being humane; people as a whole
items.example: Humanity carries both the kind sense and the collective sense.
items.exampleCN: humanity 兼含仁厚与总体两义。

items.example: The prefix denies either the species or the warmth.
items.exampleCN: 该前缀否定物种义或温度义。

items.example: The prefix raises the adjective above the normal limit.
items.exampleCN: 该前缀把形容词抬到常人限度之上。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a verb of making.
items.exampleCN: 该后缀把形容词变成「使成为」的动词。

items.example: The prefix reverses the making.
items.exampleCN: 该前缀把「使成为」反过来。

items.meaning: one who acts for human welfare
items.example: The longer ending names a commitment, not a species.
items.exampleCN: 较长的词尾指的是一种承诺，而非物种。

definition_zh: 人类（总称）；仁厚；人性；人文学科
definition_en: people taken as a whole, or the quality of being kind and civilized
core_image: 洪水退去后的渡口：撑船的人不问来处，只把人一个个接上岸
scene: 洪水退去，邻村的人撑船来接陌生人，谁也不登记姓名。The rescuers showed a humanity that no border could contain.
sceneCN: 这里「仁厚」指待人以怜悯与尊重的品质（第 2 个义项：仁厚品质）；句意为救援者表现出一种任何边界都装不下的仁厚。

pos.zh: 人类（总称，不可数）；仁厚；人性；复数 humanities 指人文学科

derivatives.zh: humanity 的形容词基座：拉丁 humanus「人的」→ 人的；人
humanus 经法语较早借入 → 仁慈的（语义偏移：只留「善待」一义）
humane + -ly → 以仁慈的方式
human + -ism（主义）→ 人文主义（语义偏移：以人的学问与价值为中心）
humanism + -ist → 人文主义者
humanity + -arian → 人道主义的；人道主义者
in-（否定）+ humanity → 无人性；残忍（语义偏移：仁厚的反面）
humanity 的复数 → 人文学科（语义偏移：从「人性」到「研究人的表达的那些学问」）

senses.title: People as a whole
senses.titleCN: 人类总称：作为一个整体的全体人
senses.definition: human beings considered collectively, especially in relation to their future or survival
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体来看的全体人，尤就未来与存续而言
senses.example: The rescuers showed a humanity that no border could contain.
senses.exampleCN: 救援者表现出一种任何边界都装不下的仁厚。
senses.why: Latin humanitas could name the whole of the human race as well as its better qualities; English kept both, so the same word can mean everyone and the best in everyone.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 humanitas 既能指整个人类，也能指人较好的品质；英语两义都保留，因此同一个词既可指所有人，也可指人身上最好的部分。

senses.title: Kindness toward others
senses.titleCN: 仁厚：待人的怜悯与尊重
senses.definition: the quality of treating others with compassion and respect
senses.definitionCN: 以怜悯与尊重对待他人的品质
senses.example: She met the prisoners with a humanity the guards had forgotten.
senses.exampleCN: 她以看守们已经忘掉的仁厚对待囚犯。
senses.why: Cicero used humanitas for the refinement that makes a person fit company for others; the modern sense narrows that to warmth of treatment.
senses.whyCN: 西塞罗用 humanitas 指使人适于与人相处的教养；现代义把这层教养收窄为待人时的温度。

senses.title: Human nature
senses.titleCN: 人性：人共有的本性
senses.definition: the shared nature or condition of human beings
senses.definitionCN: 人所共有的本性或处境
senses.example: The story tests whether humanity is generous when no one is watching.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事追问：无人看见时，人性是否仍然宽厚。
senses.why: If humanitas is what belongs to homo, it can name the common constitution of people rather than their deeds; philosophers then argue about how much of it is fixed.
senses.whyCN: 若 humanitas 是「属于人」的东西，它就可以指人共有的构造，而非具体行为；哲学家由此争论其中多少是固定的。

senses.title: The humanities
senses.titleCN: 人文学科：研究人的表达的那些学问
senses.definition: the branches of learning that study human expression, such as literature, history and philosophy
senses.definitionCN: 研究人类表达的诸学问，如文学、历史与哲学
senses.example: He moved from law into the humanities and never regretted it.
senses.exampleCN: 他从法律转向人文学科，从未后悔。
senses.why: Renaissance Latin used literae humaniores, 'the more human letters'; the plural humanities kept that claim that such studies make a person more fully human.
senses.whyCN: 文艺复兴拉丁语说 literae humaniores「更有人味的文字」；复数 humanities 保留了这一主张：这些学问使人更像人。

senses.title: Civilized refinement
senses.titleCN: 教养：使人文雅有礼的修养
senses.definition: cultivated courtesy and refinement of manner
senses.definitionCN: 文雅有礼的教养与举止
senses.example: His humanity showed in how he disagreed: always with the other person's reasons stated first.
senses.exampleCN: 他的教养体现在他如何表示异议：总先把对方的理由说清。
senses.why: This is Cicero's original weight: humanitas as the polish that separates a citizen from a brute, closer to education than to emotion.
senses.whyCN: 这是西塞罗原本的分量：humanitas 是使公民区别于野蛮人的修养，更近于教育而非情感。

senses.title: Frailty and mortality
senses.titleCN: 人的脆弱：会错、会老、会死的处境
senses.definition: the weakness and mortality that belong to being a person
senses.definitionCN: 作为人所固有的软弱、易错与必死
senses.example: The film strips the general of his medals and leaves him his humanity.
senses.exampleCN: 影片剥去将军的勋章，只留下他作为人的脆弱。
senses.why: Because humanitas marks what belongs to people, it also marks what people cannot escape; the word can console as easily as it can praise.
senses.whyCN: 因为 humanitas 标记属于人的东西，它也标记人逃不掉的东西；这个词既能称赞，也能安慰。

senses.title: Mercy in practice
senses.titleCN: 实践中的怜悯：战争与灾难中的底线
senses.definition: the minimum of mercy that people owe one another even in conflict
senses.definitionCN: 即便在冲突中也应给人的最低限度的怜悯
senses.example: The laws of humanity forbid leaving the wounded without water.
senses.exampleCN: 人道法则禁止让伤员无水可饮。
senses.why: Law borrowed the word for a floor below which conduct may not fall: humanity is what remains owed when every other claim has been set aside.
senses.whyCN: 法律借用这个词来指行为不可跌破的底线：当其他主张都被搁置时，仍欠人的那一份就是 humanity。

senses.title: A shared moral community
senses.titleCN: 共同的道义共同体：人对人的相互归属
senses.definition: the sense that all people belong to one another and owe one another something
senses.definitionCN: 一切人对彼此都有归属与亏欠的意识
senses.example: The appeal was made in the name of a humanity that includes the enemy.
senses.exampleCN: 这项呼吁以包含敌人的那份人类共同体之名提出。
senses.why: Because humanitas could name the whole race, the collective sense stretches into a moral claim: if the word covers everyone, everyone is inside the circle of obligation, including the enemy.
senses.whyCN: 由于 humanitas 本可指整个族类，集体义便伸展为一种道义主张：既然这个词涵盖所有人，所有人就都在义务圈内，包括敌人。

senses.title: The human side of an institution
senses.titleCN: 机构中的人情一面：制度里的人
senses.definition: the human, personal side of an institution or a system
senses.definitionCN: 机构或制度中属于人的、个人的一面
senses.example: The ward kept its humanity by letting families stay after hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这间病房靠允许家属夜间留下，保住了它的人情。
senses.why: When an institution is said to have lost its humanity, its warmth is being separated from its rules; the collective noun is reused for the quality that rules cannot supply.
senses.whyCN: 当说某机构失去人情时，是把温度从规则里剥离出来；集体名词被借来指规则无法提供的那份品质。

intro.en: Humanity is Cicero's Latin abstract noun, famous as his rendering of a Greek educational ideal; its later split into 'everyone' and 'the better in everyone' happened in English.
intro.cn: humanity 是西塞罗的拉丁抽象名词，以翻译希腊教育理想而著名；后来「所有人」与「人身上最好的部分」两义的分裂发生在英语里。

items.en: Humanus 'human, kind' was the adjective of homo 'person'; both 'belonging to people' and 'good to people' were already inside it.
items.cn: humanus「人的、仁厚的」是 homo「人」的形容词；「属于人」与「善待人的」两义本已在其中。

items.en: Humanitas named human nature, humane feeling and cultivated learning at once; the abstraction was formed with -itas, the ending that makes a quality noun.
items.cn: humanitas 同时指人性、仁厚与教养；这一抽象由 -itas 构成，那是把形容词变成品质名词的词尾。

items.en: Cicero used humanitas for the Greek paideia, the training that makes a person fully human; the pairing is generally accepted, though it is Cicero's choice rather than a literal translation.
items.cn: 西塞罗用 humanitas 对译希腊 paideia，即使人成为完整之人的教养；这一配对一般被接受，但它是西塞罗的选用，而非逐字直译。

items.en: Old French humanite carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first in the sense of human nature and kind feeling.
items.cn: 古法语 humanite 在 14 世纪把这个名词带入英语，最初指人性与仁厚之情。

items.en: The collective sense 'all people' is a later English development, and the plural humanities took over the educational sense in the Renaissance.
items.cn: 「全体人」的集体义是英语后来发展出的；复数 humanities 在文艺复兴时期接过了教育义。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the origin of homo behind humanus is unsettled, and the humus 'earth' reading is a hypothesis; no pre-Latin form is attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：humanus 背后的 homo 来源未定，与 humus「土地」的读法是假说；拉丁语之前的形式无书证。

note.en: Group one holds the same-family words whose senses overlap just enough to be confused; group two holds the collective nouns for people.
note.cn: 第一组是同族词，词义交叠到刚好容易混；第二组是指全体人的集体名词。

entries.definition: The older French-shaped borrowing: compassionate and merciful, with no collective meaning at all.
entries.definitionCN: 较早的法国形状借词：仁慈宽厚，完全没有集体义。

entries.definition: The neutral adjective and the countable noun; it never means people as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 中性形容词与可数名词；从不指全体人。

entries.definition: The outlook that places human values and human learning at the centre; it is a programme, not a feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 把人的价值与学问置于中心的取向；是一套主张，不是一种情感。

entries.definition: The negation of the kind sense: cruelty, the absence of what people owe one another.
entries.definitionCN: 仁厚义的反面：残忍，人不再亏欠彼此。

entries.definition: A gender-neutral collective noun for the species; it carries no evaluative shade.
entries.definitionCN: 指物种的中性集体名词；不带评价色彩。

entries.definition: The traditional collective noun, now often avoided because its second element once meant 'man'.
entries.definitionCN: 传统的集体名词，因第二成分曾指「男人」，今常被回避。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for persons, used with numbers; humanity never takes a number.
entries.definitionCN: 指人的日常词，可与数目连用；humanity 从不用数目。

entries.definition: The organized social life of a large society; it overlaps with the refinement sense but not with the collective one.
entries.definitionCN: 大型社会的有组织生活；与教养义部分重叠，但与总称义无关。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin layers, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁层次、真实派生词与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin humanitas packed three things: human nature, kind feeling and cultivated learning; English gave each a separate life.
normal.cn: 拉丁 humanitas 装了三样东西：人性、仁厚与教养；英语让每一义各自生活。

normal.en: The family runs human, humane, humanity, humanities, humanism, humanitarian, inhumanity.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 human、humane、humanity、humanities、humanism、humanitarian、inhumanity。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the collective sense: a crime against humanity, the future of humanity.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出总称义：反人类罪、人类的未来。

normal.en: The plural humanities is a Renaissance inheritance: literae humaniores, the more human letters.
normal.cn: 复数 humanities 是文艺复兴的遗产：literae humaniores，更有人味的文字。

normal.en: Cicero is the hinge: paideia became humanitas, and education became the measure of a person.
normal.cn: 西塞罗是关键：paideia 变成 humanitas，教养成了衡量人的尺度。

abstract.en: Picture a ferry that asks no name and takes everyone aboard.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘不问姓名、把所有人都载上的渡船。

abstract.en: Picture a library where the shelves are labelled with what they make people become.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，书架标着它们使人成为什么。

abstract.en: Picture a law that keeps one bare promise when every other promise has failed.
abstract.cn: 想象一条法律，在其他承诺都失效时仍守着一个最低承诺。

examples.en: The report treated water as a matter of common humanity, not of charity.
examples.cn: 报告把水视为共同人性之事，而非施舍。

examples.en: Reading history is part of the humanities, and it is also an argument about humanity.
examples.cn: 读历史属于人文学科，同时也是一场关于人性的论证。

examples.en: No institution keeps its humanity by accident; someone has to insist on it.
examples.cn: 没有哪个机构是偶然保住人情的；总得有人坚持。

dict_mnemonic.text: human（人的）+ ity（性质）＝ 人的性质，既指全体人，也指仁厚；记「一个词管两个极端：所有人与最好的人」。

root: 拉丁 humanitas「人性、仁厚、教养」，由 humanus「人的」+ -itas（品质名词词尾）构成；humanus 出自 homo「人」，homo 更深来源不确定，与 humus「土地」的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses divide one abstraction into two families: a collective family (all people, a shared moral community, the human side of an institution) and a quality family (kindness, refinement, frailty, mercy, and the studies that claim to cultivate it).
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项把同一个抽象分成两族：集体一族（全体人、共同道义体、机构中的人情）与品质一族（仁厚、教养、脆弱、怜悯，以及自称能培养它的那些学问）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ferry landing after a flood, where nobody asks where anyone is from.
core.cn: 核心意象：洪水后的渡口，没有人问谁从哪里来。

branches.en: EVERYONE AND WHAT EVERYONE IS: the collective, then the nature shared by it.
branches.cn: 所有人，以及所有人共有的东西：先是全体，再是共有的本性。

branches.en: WARMTH AND ITS POLISH: compassion in action, and the courtesy that education adds.
branches.cn: 温度与它的打磨：行动中的怜悯，以及教养添上的礼节。

branches.en: THE STUDIES THAT CLAIM IT: the humanities as the inheritors of paideia.
branches.cn: 自称能培养它的学问：人文学科作为 paideia 的继承者。

branches.en: THE LOW END AND THE FLOOR: frailty that cannot be avoided, and mercy that cannot be withheld.
branches.cn: 低处与底线：无法避免的脆弱，与不可扣留的怜悯。

branches.en: COMMUNITY AND INSTITUTIONS: a bond that includes the enemy, and the warmth rules cannot supply.
branches.cn: 共同体与机构：包含敌人的纽带，以及规则无法提供的温度。

intro.en: Humanity is an abstract noun built on a Latin adjective with a Latin quality ending, and the same stem supports a large family with two competing borrowings.
intro.cn: humanity 是由拉丁形容词加拉丁品质词尾构成的抽象名词，同一词干支撑一大族词，其中有两次相互竞争的借入。

latinIntro.en: Latin homo supplies the stem, humanus the adjective, and -itas the quality noun; English also holds the earlier French-shaped humane beside the later Latin-shaped human.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 homo 提供词干，humanus 提供形容词，-itas 构成品质名词；英语里较早的法国形状 humane 与较晚的拉丁形状 human 并存。

items.example: The stem carries both the neutral and the warm sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干兼含中性义与温度义。

items.example: The ending turns human into an abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把 human 变成抽象名词。

items.meaning: the quality of being human; people collectively
items.example: Humanity carries both families of sense.
items.exampleCN: humanity 兼含两族义项。

items.structure: humanus through Old French, an earlier borrowing
items.example: Humane split off with only the warm sense.
items.exampleCN: humane 分出去后只带温度义。

items.example: Human kept the neutral sense and the countable noun.
items.exampleCN: human 保留中性义与可数名词用法。

items.meaning: the outlook centred on human values
items.example: The movement took the educational sense of humanity.
items.exampleCN: 这场运动接过了 humanity 的教育义。

items.example: The ending marks adherence to a programme.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾标记对一套主张的信奉。

items.meaning: one who acts for human welfare
items.example: The ending marks a commitment to relief.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾标记对救助的承诺。

items.example: The prefix reverses the quality noun.
items.exampleCN: 该前缀把品质名词反转。

items.example: The plural took over the educational sense.
items.exampleCN: 复数接过了教育义。

latinEntries.structure: paideia (Greek noun, f., first declension, used in Latin texts)

definition_zh: 人类；作为整体的全体人（中性集体称谓）
definition_en: human beings taken collectively, used as a neutral term for the species
core_image: 一根冰芯与一片陶片被摆在同一张长桌上，标签写着同一个年份，却来自地球两端
scene: 冰芯与陶片被并排放在同一张长桌上，解说员说这两样记的是同一笔账。Climate records trapped in ice now count as part of the archive of humankind.
sceneCN: 这里「人类」指作为整体的全体人（第 1 个义项：全体人的集体称谓）；句意为封在冰里的气候记录如今也算作人类档案的一部分。

pos.zh: 人类（不可数集体名词，中性语体；不作复数）

derivatives.zh: humankind 的前件：拉丁 humanus「人的」→ 人的；人
古英语 gecynd「天性、族类」→ 种类；族类（语义偏移：从「天性」到「一类」）
古英语 mancynn「人的族类」→ 人类（语义偏移：第二成分与 man 的阳性用法合并，今多被回避）
human + -ity → 人类；仁厚（语义偏移：兼指全体与品质）
humanus 经法语与拉丁两次借入 → 人的

senses.title: All people collectively
senses.titleCN: 全体人：作为一个整体的集体称谓
senses.definition: human beings considered as one collective, especially in statements about the species
senses.definitionCN: 被当作一个集体的全体人，尤用于关于物种的陈述
senses.example: Climate records trapped in ice now count as part of the archive of humankind.
senses.exampleCN: 封在冰里的气候记录如今也算作人类档案的一部分。
senses.why: Human supplies the species and kind supplies the class; the compound says 'the class of people' in one word, which is why it can stand as the subject of a sentence about everyone.
senses.whyCN: human 提供物种，kind 提供「类」；这个复合词用一个词说出「人这一类」，因此能在一句关于所有人的话里充当主语。

senses.title: The species as a biological entity
senses.titleCN: 作为物种：生物学上的一个单位
senses.definition: the species Homo sapiens treated as a single biological population
senses.definitionCN: 被当作单一生物种群的智人
senses.example: A virus can spread through humankind faster than any border can close.
senses.exampleCN: 病毒穿越人类的速度比任何边界关闭得都快。
senses.why: Once the compound names a class, it can be handed to biology, where a class of people is simply one species with one gene pool.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个复合词命名一个类，便可交给生物学使用；在那里，「人这一类」就是拥有一个基因库的一个物种。

senses.title: The subject of history
senses.titleCN: 历史的主体：文明进程的承担者
senses.definition: people viewed as the collective agent of history and invention
senses.definitionCN: 被看作历史与发明之集体承担者的人
senses.example: Every tool in the case belongs to the long apprenticeship of humankind.
senses.exampleCN: 柜里的每一件工具都属于人类漫长的学徒期。
senses.why: History needs a singular actor for long processes; humankind supplies an actor that is not a nation, a class or a leader.
senses.whyCN: 历史需要为长进程找一个单数行动者；humankind 提供的行动者不是国家、阶级或领袖。

senses.title: Common fate and survival
senses.titleCN: 共同命运：存续与未来的共同承担
senses.definition: the shared stake people have in survival and in what comes next
senses.definitionCN: 人在存续与未来上所共有的利害
senses.example: The treaty was written as a promise to humankind, not to its signatories.
senses.exampleCN: 这份条约写成了对人类的承诺，而不是对签署国的承诺。
senses.why: If the word names everyone, then risks that reach everyone can be addressed to it; the compound became the natural addressee of climate and pandemic arguments.
senses.whyCN: 若这个词指所有人，则波及所有人的风险就可以向它发话；这个复合词于是成了气候与疫病论证的天然受话者。

senses.title: A moral community
senses.titleCN: 道义共同体：人对彼此的义务
senses.definition: all people regarded as bound by obligations to one another
senses.definitionCN: 被视为对彼此负有义务的全体人
senses.example: The argument appealed to a duty owed to humankind rather than to neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 这项论证诉诸对人类的义务，而不是对邻人的义务。
senses.why: Because kind also means a class or a family, the compound can carry a family's mutual obligation and stretch it to the widest possible kinship.
senses.whyCN: 因为 kind 也指一类或一族，这个复合词能带着家族式的相互义务，并把它拉到最宽的亲属范围。

senses.title: The human stock in anthropology
senses.titleCN: 人类这一支：谱系意义上的共同祖先群体
senses.definition: the human lineage viewed as one stock descended from shared ancestors
senses.definitionCN: 被视为出自共同祖先的单一人类谱系
senses.example: Geneticists trace the migrations of humankind from a single African population.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传学家追索人类从单一非洲种群开始的迁徙。
senses.why: Anthropology and genetics need a word for the lineage, not for a culture; humankind fits because it names the stock rather than any of its societies.
senses.whyCN: 人类学与遗传学需要一个指谱系、而非指文化的词；humankind 正合适，因为它命名的是这一支，而非其中任何一个社会。

senses.title: Emphatic rhetorical use
senses.titleCN: 修辞上的强调：把范围推到极限
senses.definition: used in appeals to stress that no group is excluded
senses.definitionCN: 在呼吁中强调不排除任何群体
senses.example: The letter began with a phrase meant to include all humankind and then named only one continent.
senses.exampleCN: 这封公开信开头一句意在涵盖全人类，随后却只点了一个大陆。
senses.why: Because it is slightly formal, the compound suits declarations; the same breadth that makes it useful in appeals makes it easy to abuse.
senses.whyCN: 由于语体略正式，这个复合词适合宣言；使它适用于呼吁的那份广度，也使它容易被滥用。

senses.title: Rational creatures in older discourse
senses.titleCN: 旧时论述中的理性造物：与神相对的受造者
senses.definition: people considered as rational created beings, in older religious and philosophical writing
senses.definitionCN: 旧时宗教与哲学论述中作为理性受造者的人
senses.example: Older sermons addressed humankind as a creature that must account for its reason.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的布道把人类当作须为自己的理性交账的受造者。
senses.why: Before the modern biological sense, the compound's parts pointed to a class defined by nature or creation, so it could stand opposite divinity.
senses.whyCN: 在现代生物学义之前，复合词的两部分指向一个由天性或受造而定的类，因此能与神性相对。

intro.en: Humankind is not a Latin inheritance but an English compound, deliberately assembled in the nineteenth century beside the older mankind; kind is native English, human is Latin-derived.
intro.cn: humankind 不是拉丁遗产，而是英语复合词，于 19 世纪有意在更早的 mankind 之外组装而成；kind 是英语本族词，human 则来自拉丁。

items.en: Gecynd meant 'nature, kind, race', from the root of cynn 'family, tribe'; the modern kind keeps that sense of a class in such phrases as what kind of.
items.cn: gecynd 意为「天性、种类、族类」，出自 cynn「家族、部族」的词根；现代 kind 在「哪一种」这类说法里仍保留「类」的意思。

items.en: Humanus, the adjective of homo 'person', entered English as human and supplied the first element of the compound.
items.cn: humanus 是 homo「人」的形容词，作为 human 进入英语，并提供复合词的前件。

items.en: Mancyn, literally 'the kind of man', had named the race since before the Norman conquest and became the modern mankind.
items.cn: mancyn 字面为「人的族类」，自诺曼征服之前就指人类，后来成为现代的 mankind。

items.en: Humankind was formed by replacing the first element of mankind with human, at a time when man was increasingly felt to exclude women; the word appears in print from the nineteenth century.
items.cn: humankind 是把 mankind 的前件换成 human 而构成，当时 man 越来越被认为排除了女性；该词自 19 世纪见于印刷品。

items.en: In the twentieth century the compound became the standard neutral word in policy, science and declarations about the species.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪，这个复合词成为政策、科学与物种宣言中的标准中性词。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): no single first citation is agreed for the compound, and the pre-English origin of homo behind human remains unsettled, with the humus 'earth' reading a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个复合词没有公认的最早书证；human 背后的 homo 在英语之前来源未定，与 humus「土地」的读法是假说。

note.en: Group one holds the collective nouns that compete directly with humankind; group two holds the words for the species or for people as subjects.
note.cn: 第一组是直接与 humankind 竞争的集体名词；第二组是指物种或以人为主体的词。

entries.definition: The inherited collective noun, increasingly avoided because its first element also means 'adult male'.
entries.definitionCN: 承继而来的集体名词，因前件也指「成年男性」而日渐被回避。

entries.definition: Also means all people, but it additionally means kindness and carries the humanities in the plural.
entries.definitionCN: 也指全体人，但另含仁厚义，复数还指人文学科。

entries.definition: A plainer phrase for the species, common in older writing and in sports commentary.
entries.definitionCN: 指物种的更朴素说法，旧文与体育解说中常见。

entries.definition: The plural of the individual noun: it counts people rather than naming their class.
entries.definitionCN: 个体名词的复数：数人，而非命名人的类。

entries.definition: The technical label for humans as one interbreeding population; colder but more precise.
entries.definitionCN: 把人作为一个可杂交种群的技术称谓；更冷峻也更精确。

entries.definition: The people of a polity considered as an audience or a body of citizens, far narrower than the species.
entries.definitionCN: 把政治共同体中的人视为受众或公民总体，范围远窄于物种。

entries.definition: People considered as an organised system of institutions, not as a biological class.
entries.definitionCN: 把人视为有组织的制度体系，而非生物类别。

entries.definition: A countable set of people in a defined area or category, the unit of demographic work.
entries.definitionCN: 在限定地区或类别中可计数的人群，是人口统计的单位。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds, real origins and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合方式、真实来源与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: human + kind, where kind is the native word for a class or a race, as in what kind of.
normal.cn: human + kind，kind 是表示类或族的本族词，如「哪一种」里的 kind。

normal.en: The word was assembled to replace mankind at a time when man was felt to leave women out.
normal.cn: 这个词是为取代 mankind 而组装的，当时 man 被认为把女性排除在外。

normal.en: The family runs human, humanity, mankind, humankind, human race, human being.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 human、humanity、mankind、humankind、human race、human being。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: the future of humankind, a threat to humankind, for all humankind.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：人类的未来、对人类的威胁、为了全人类。

normal.en: It takes a singular verb: humankind is, not humankind are.
normal.cn: 它接单数谓语，而非复数谓语。

abstract.en: Picture one ledger in which every country has the same signature line.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账，每个国家都在同一行签名。

abstract.en: Picture a family tree so wide that the page must be folded many times.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵宽到纸要折很多次的家谱。

abstract.en: Picture a word built by swapping one brick out of an old wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词，是从一堵旧墙上换下一块砖建成的。

examples.en: The exhibition framed the ice core as a document of humankind.
examples.cn: 展览把这根冰芯呈现为一份人类文献。

examples.en: No single generation owns the climate; it is held in trust for humankind.
examples.cn: 没有哪一代人拥有气候；它是为人类代管的。

examples.en: The word humankind avoids the old objection to mankind without changing the meaning.
examples.cn: humankind 一词避开了对 mankind 的旧异议，而含义不变。

dict_mnemonic.text: human（人的）+ kind（类）＝ 人这一类；记「换下一块旧砖：mankind 的 man 换成 human」。

root: 英语复合词：human（拉丁 humanus「人的」，出自 homo「人」）+ kind（古英语 gecynd「天性、族类」）；19 世纪为回避 mankind 的阳性前件而造。homo 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one compound from a simple class to a formal addressee: everyone, the species, the actor of history, a shared fate, a moral community, the human lineage, a rhetorical breadth and the older rational creature.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着一个复合词从一个简单的类走到正式的受话者：全体人、物种、历史的主体、共同命运、道义共同体、人类谱系、修辞上的广度，以及旧时的理性造物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an ice core and a potsherd on one long table, labelled with the same year though they come from opposite ends of the earth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根冰芯与一片陶片摆在同一张长桌上，标签是同一年份，却来自地球两端。

branches.en: CLASS AND SPECIES: the plain collective, then the same class handed to biology.
branches.cn: 类与物种：先是朴素的集体，再把同一个类交给生物学。

branches.en: LONG PROCESSES: history's singular actor, and the lineage traced by genes.
branches.cn: 长进程：历史的单数行动者，以及由基因追出的谱系。

branches.en: WHAT IS OWED: a fate no group can opt out of, and an obligation that reaches the enemy.
branches.cn: 所欠之物：没有哪个群体能退出的命运，以及延伸到敌人的义务。

branches.en: THE DECLARATION TONE: the breadth that suits appeals and invites abuse.
branches.cn: 宣言腔：适合呼吁的那份广度，也招致滥用。

branches.en: THE OLDER READING: a class defined by creation, standing opposite the divine.
branches.cn: 更早的读法：由受造而定的类，与神性相对。

intro.en: The word is a native-English compound whose first element is Latin-derived and whose second element is inherited Old English, so it mixes two systems openly.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语本族复合词，前件来自拉丁，后件承自古老英语，两套系统公开混在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin humanus supplies the first element through human; Old English gecynd supplies the second through kind. Latin contributes no second element here, since kind is native.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 humanus 经 human 提供前件；古英语 gecynd 经 kind 提供后件。拉丁语在此不提供后件，因为 kind 是本族词。

items.example: The first element names the species.
items.exampleCN: 前件命名物种。

items.example: The second element names the class.
items.exampleCN: 后件命名类别。

items.example: The compound names the class in one word.
items.exampleCN: 复合词用一个词命名这个类。

items.example: The older compound used man for the species.
items.exampleCN: 旧复合词用 man 指物种。

items.example: Humanity overlaps the collective sense.
items.exampleCN: humanity 与集体义重叠。

items.example: The possessive marks what belongs to the whole class.
items.exampleCN: 所有格标记属于整个类的东西。

items.example: The adverb modifies how something is done.
items.exampleCN: 副词修饰做法。

items.example: The doublet supplies the warm sense.
items.exampleCN: 同源双式词提供温度义。

items.example: The suffix describes shape, not class.
items.exampleCN: 该后缀描述形状，而非类别。

definition_zh: 人类演化；人类这一支在体质、行为与文化上的长期演变
definition_en: the long-term biological and cultural change of the human lineage
core_image: 展厅墙上一排逐渐直立的骨架，末端那具却回头看着起点
scene: 展厅墙上画着一条从左到右越来越直的线，孩子指着末端问那是谁。Human evolution is usually told as a single line, although the evidence looks more like a bush.
sceneCN: 这里「人类演化」指人类这一支的长期演变过程（第 1 个义项：作为整体过程）；句意为人类演化常被讲成一条直线，尽管证据看起来更像一丛灌木。

pos.zh: 人类演化（不可数，指过程或研究领域；亦可作 human evolution studies 指多类研究）

collocations.phrase: the fossil record of human evolution

derivatives.zh: 拉丁 evolutio「展开」（来自 evolvere「卷开」）→ 演化；进化（语义偏移：从「把书卷展开」到「形态逐代展开」）
e-（向外）+ volvere（拉丁「卷、转」）→ 演化；逐渐形成
evolution + -ary（关系形容词后缀）→ 演化的；进化论的
evolution + -ist → 演化论者（语义偏移：持演化解释的人）
paleo-（希腊 palaios「古老」）+ anthropology → 古人类学：以化石研究人类演化
拉丁 homo（人）+ -ini（族级分类词尾）→ 人族成员：人类演化线上的物种

senses.title: The process as a whole
senses.titleCN: 作为整体过程：人类这一支的长期变化
senses.definition: the whole sequence of biological and behavioural change in the human lineage
senses.definitionCN: 人类谱系在体质与行为上的整段变化
senses.example: Human evolution is usually told as a single line, although the evidence looks more like a bush.
senses.exampleCN: 人类演化常被讲成一条直线，尽管证据看起来更像一丛灌木。
senses.why: Evolution comes from Latin evolvere, 'to unroll', and humanus marks the lineage; the phrase therefore names the unrolling of the human line through time.
senses.whyCN: evolution 出自拉丁 evolvere「展开、卷开」，humanus 标记这一谱系；因此短语指人类这一支随时间展开的过程。

senses.title: The research field
senses.titleCN: 作为研究领域：专门研究这段过程的学科
senses.definition: the interdisciplinary field that investigates that process
senses.definitionCN: 专门考察这一过程的交叉学科
senses.example: Human evolution is now studied with genetics as much as with calipers.
senses.exampleCN: 如今研究人类演化，用遗传学不比用卡尺少。
senses.why: A process so long that nobody can watch it must be reconstructed, and reconstruction became a profession with its own journals.
senses.whyCN: 这段过程长到无人能亲眼看见，只能重建，而重建变成了一门有自己的期刊的职业。

senses.title: The fossil record
senses.titleCN: 作为化石记录：可被读出的那串证据
senses.definition: the ordered series of fossils from which the process is read
senses.definitionCN: 据以读出这段过程的有序化石序列
senses.example: The fossil record of human evolution is rich in jaws and poor in pelves.
senses.exampleCN: 人类演化的化石记录里，下颌骨很多，骨盆很少。
senses.why: A process is invisible; a record is readable. English uses the phrase for the evidence itself whenever the argument turns on what has actually been found.
senses.whyCN: 过程看不见，记录可读。每当论证取决于实际挖到了什么，英语就用这个短语指证据本身。

senses.title: The rise of bipedalism
senses.titleCN: 直立行走的出现：最早的关键转变
senses.definition: the shift to habitual walking on two legs, the earliest major change in the lineage
senses.definitionCN: 转为常态两足行走，是谱系中最早的重大转变
senses.example: Human evolution is often dated from a pelvis that could no longer be mistaken for an ape's.
senses.exampleCN: 人类演化常从一个不再会被误认为猿类的骨盆开始算起。
senses.why: Freeing the hands preceded enlarging the brain, so the first chapter of the story is a change in gait rather than in intelligence.
senses.whyCN: 解放双手先于扩大脑容量，因此这个故事的第一章是步态的改变，而不是智力的改变。

senses.title: The expansion of the brain
senses.titleCN: 脑的扩大：颅容量与认知的变化
senses.definition: the increase in brain size and complexity across the lineage
senses.definitionCN: 谱系中脑容量与复杂度的增加
senses.example: Human evolution includes a brain that tripled while the jaw shrank.
senses.exampleCN: 人类演化包括一个增大到三倍、同时下颌缩小的脑。
senses.why: Encephalization is the second classic chapter: it is measurable from skulls, which is why it entered the story so early and so prominently.
senses.whyCN: 脑化是第二个经典章节：它可从颅骨测量，所以很早就显眼地进入了这个故事。

senses.title: Tools and culture as part of the process
senses.titleCN: 工具与文化：作为演化的一部分
senses.definition: the inclusion of toolmaking, fire and social learning in the evolutionary account
senses.definitionCN: 把工具制作、用火与社会性学习纳入演化叙述
senses.example: Human evolution cannot be told without stone, because stone carries behaviour.
senses.exampleCN: 讲人类演化离不开石头，因为石头承载着行为。
senses.why: Gene-culture coevolution is the modern correction: culture is not a garnish on the biology but a pressure acting back on it.
senses.whyCN: 基因与文化的共同演化是现代修正：文化不是生物学的装饰，而是反作用于生物学的压力。

senses.title: Migration and population history
senses.titleCN: 迁徙与群体史：扩散、混合与基因流
senses.definition: the dispersal of populations and the mixing of lineages across continents
senses.definitionCN: 人群的扩散与谱系在各大洲间的混合
senses.example: Human evolution now includes several waves out of Africa and repeated interbreeding.
senses.exampleCN: 人类演化如今包括数次走出非洲的浪潮与反复的杂交。
senses.why: Once genetics entered the field, the story stopped being a family tree and became a set of branching, rejoining populations.
senses.whyCN: 遗传学进入之后，这个故事不再是家谱，而是一组分叉又汇合的人群。

senses.title: The evolution of behaviour and cooperation
senses.titleCN: 行为与合作：社会性的演化
senses.definition: the evolutionary account of social life, care and cooperation
senses.definitionCN: 对社会生活、照料与合作的演化解释
senses.example: Human evolution is also the history of a species that raises children in groups.
senses.exampleCN: 人类演化也是一个成群抚养孩子的物种的历史。
senses.why: Behaviour leaves fewer fossils than bone does, so this chapter is argued from living primates, campsites and stone; it is the most contested part of the story.
senses.whyCN: 行为留下的化石比骨头少，因此这一章要靠现生灵长类、营地与石器来论证；它是故事里争议最大的部分。

senses.title: The public narrative
senses.titleCN: 公共叙事：教科书与展厅讲的版本
senses.definition: the simplified story presented in museums, textbooks and documentaries
senses.definitionCN: 博物馆、教科书与纪录片所呈现的简化故事
senses.example: The human evolution on the museum wall ends with a figure carrying a briefcase.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆墙上的人类演化以一个人提着公文包的形象收尾。
senses.why: Any long process must be edited to be told; the public version is a real sense of the phrase, and its simplifications are what specialists argue with.
senses.whyCN: 任何漫长的过程都必须经过剪辑才能讲述；公共版本是这个短语的一个真实义项，而它的简化正是专家争论的对象。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin-derived adjective for the human line to a Latin noun for unrolling; the modern sense of the noun is a nineteenth-century English development.
intro.cn: 这个短语把指人类谱系的拉丁来源形容词接在拉丁语「展开」名词上；名词的现代义是 19 世纪英语的发展。

items.en: Humanus, the adjective of homo 'person', reached English as human and formed the phrase's first element; the deeper origin of homo is unsettled.
items.cn: humanus 是 homo「人」的形容词，作为 human 进入英语，成为短语前件；homo 的更深来源未定。

items.en: Evolvere meant 'to roll out, unroll', built on ex- 'out' plus volvere 'to roll'. The image is physical: a scroll is opened so that what was folded can be read in order.
items.cn: evolvere 意为「展开、卷开」，由 ex-「向外」加 volvere「卷、转」构成。意象是具体的：把书卷打开，原本折叠的内容才能按序读出。

items.en: Evolutio named the act of unrolling, especially of a book; it carried no biological sense in classical Latin.
items.cn: evolutio 指展开的动作，尤指展开书卷；在古典拉丁语中没有生物学含义。

items.en: In the nineteenth century evolution acquired the sense of gradual change of species, and the phrase human evolution followed the general acceptance of that idea.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，evolution 获得物种逐渐变化的含义；人类演化这一短语随该观念的普遍接受而出现。

items.en: Genetics, radiometric dating and comparative anatomy turned the phrase into a research programme with its own evidence standards.
items.cn: 遗传学、放射性定年与比较解剖学把这个短语变成有自身证据标准的研究纲领。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact phrase has no agreed first citation, and the origin of homo behind humanus is unknown, with the humus 'earth' reading a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这一确切短语没有公认的最早书证；humanus 背后的 homo 来源不明，与 humus「土地」的读法是假说。

note.en: Group one holds the phrases most easily swapped for the whole process; group two holds the mechanisms and neighbouring processes.
note.cn: 第一组是最容易被换用来指整个过程的短语；第二组是机制与邻近过程。

entries.definition: The early divergence and first members of the lineage; it names a period, while evolution names the whole run.
entries.definitionCN: 谱系早期的分化与最早成员；它命名一个阶段，而 evolution 命名整段行程。

entries.definition: The evolutionary history of the wider family of great apes and humans, a broader scope.
entries.definitionCN: 更宽的人科（大猿与人类）的演化史，范围更大。

entries.definition: The field that studies the process from fossils; the phrase names the object, not the profession.
entries.definitionCN: 靠化石研究这一过程的学科；短语命名对象，而非职业。

entries.definition: The period before written records; it overlaps the recent part of evolution but is defined by documents, not genes.
entries.definitionCN: 文字记录之前的时期；与演化的晚近部分重叠，但以文献而非基因界定。

entries.definition: Change in inherited traits across generations in any population; the human case is one instance.
entries.definitionCN: 任何种群中可遗传性状的跨代变化；人类只是其中一例。

entries.definition: The differential survival of variants; it drives evolution but is not the whole of it.
entries.definitionCN: 变体差异化存活；它驱动演化，但不等于演化全部。

entries.definition: Change in learned behaviour and technology, which can outrun genetic change.
entries.definitionCN: 习得行为与技术的变化，可以跑得比基因变化快。

entries.definition: Growth and change within a single organism; it is not inherited change across generations.
entries.definitionCN: 单个生物体一生的生长与变化；不是跨代的遗传变化。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real chapter names and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的章节名与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: evolvere 'to unroll' gives the image of a scroll opened so the folded story can be read in order.
normal.cn: evolvere「展开」给出书卷被打开、折叠的故事得以按序读出的意象。

normal.en: The standard chapters are gait, brain, tools, dispersal, behaviour, and the public retelling.
normal.cn: 标准章节是步态、脑、工具、扩散、行为，以及公共复述。

normal.en: The family runs evolve, evolution, evolutionary, evolutionist, paleoanthropology, hominin.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 evolve、evolution、evolutionary、evolutionist、paleoanthropology、hominin。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: the study of human evolution, a model of human evolution, the fossil record of human evolution.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：人类演化研究、人类演化模型、人类演化的化石记录。

normal.en: The line on the wall is an edit, not the evidence; the evidence is a bush.
normal.cn: 墙上的那条线是剪辑，不是证据；证据是一丛灌木。

abstract.en: Picture a scroll that keeps unrolling and never shows the same paragraph twice.
abstract.cn: 想象一卷不断展开、从不重复同一段落的书。

abstract.en: Picture a family reunion where half the guests have not arrived yet.
abstract.cn: 想象一场家庭聚会，半数客人还没到。

abstract.en: Picture a museum poster corrected by a child with a crayon.
abstract.cn: 想象一张博物馆海报被孩子用蜡笔改过。

examples.en: Human evolution is now dated by volcanic ash layers as often as by bone shape.
examples.cn: 如今给人类演化定年，用火山灰层的次数不亚于用骨骼形态。

examples.en: The course treats human evolution as a set of populations, not a ladder.
examples.cn: 这门课把人类演化当作一组人群，而不是一架梯子。

examples.en: Claims about human evolution are easy to popularise and hard to verify.
examples.cn: 关于人类演化的主张容易普及，却难以验证。

dict_mnemonic.text: human（人的）+ evolution（展开）＝ 人类这一支随时间展开；记「不是一条线，是一丛灌木」。

root: 拉丁 humanus「人的」（homo「人」的形容词）+ evolutio「展开」，来自 evolvere（ex- + volvere「卷」）；homo 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one long unrolling: the process, the field that studies it, the record that proves it, then its chapters in order, gait, brain, tools, dispersal, behaviour, and finally the edited version told to the public.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着一段漫长的展开：过程本身、研究它的领域、证明它的记录，随后按序是各章：步态、脑、工具、扩散、行为，最后是讲给公众的剪辑版。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of skeletons that gradually stands upright, while the last one turns to look back at the first.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排逐渐直立的骨架，最末一具却回头看着第一具。

branches.en: PROCESS AND PROFESSION: the unrolling itself, then the people who reconstruct it.
branches.cn: 过程与职业：展开本身，以及重建它的人。

branches.en: WHAT CAN BE READ: a process is invisible, so the phrase can name the evidence instead.
branches.cn: 可读之物：过程看不见，短语因此可指证据。

branches.en: THE FIRST TWO CHAPTERS: standing up, then growing a larger brain.
branches.cn: 最初两章：先站起来，再长出更大的脑。

branches.en: BEHAVIOUR WRITTEN IN STONE AND GENES: tools as evidence, and populations mixing across continents.
branches.cn: 写在石头与基因里的行为：工具作为证据，人群在大陆间混合。

branches.en: THE CONTESTED AND THE SIMPLIFIED: cooperation argued from campsites, and the museum line drawn for visitors.
branches.cn: 争议之处与简化版：靠营地论证的合作，以及为观众画出的展厅直线。

intro.en: Both halves are Latin-derived, and the second half is a productive verb family in English, so the phrase can be taken apart without guessing.
intro.cn: 两半都源于拉丁，后一半在英语里是能产的动词词族，因此这个短语可以拆开而不必猜。

latinIntro.en: Latin humanus supplies the first element; Latin evolvere and evolutio supply the second, and the same verb builds involve, revolve and devolve.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 humanus 提供前件；拉丁 evolvere 与 evolutio 提供后件，同一动词还构成 involve、revolve、devolve。

items.example: The first element names whose lineage is unrolling.
items.exampleCN: 前件命名是谁的谱系在展开。

items.example: The prefix supplies the direction of the unrolling.
items.exampleCN: 前缀给出展开的方向。

items.example: The root supplies the rolling image behind evolution.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供演化背后的「卷转」意象。

items.example: The verb is the plain member of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是词族中最朴素的一员。

items.example: The noun carries the scroll image into biology.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词把书卷意象带进生物学。

items.example: The adjective marks the framework of the argument.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词标记论证的框架。

items.meaning: to wrap in, hence to include
items.example: The same root builds a word with no biological sense.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根构成一个无关生物学的词。

items.example: The prefix reverses or repeats the rolling.

items.exampleCN: 这个复合词命名读记录的那门学科。

definition_zh: 人科动物；人科成员（现含大猿与人类，旧义仅指人类一支）
definition_en: a member of the family Hominidae, which now includes great apes and humans
core_image: 抽屉里一块骨盆与一根股骨拼在一起，标签上的分类层级写着「科」
scene: 化石柜的抽屉里，一块骨盆与一根股骨被拼在一起，标签只剩地层号。The hominid pelvis in the drawer had been mislabelled for thirty years.
sceneCN: 这里「人科动物」指人科的一个化石个体（第 3 个义项：化石标本）；句意为抽屉里这块人科骨盆被错标了三十年。

pos.zh: 人科动物；人科成员（可数，复数 hominids）
人科的；人科动物特征的

derivatives.zh: 拉丁 homo（人）+ -idae（科级分类词尾）→ 人科（分类学上的科名）
拉丁 homo + -ini（族级词尾）→ 人族成员（语义偏移：层级从科降到族，范围收窄）
homo + -oid（形似）→ 人形总科的；类人猿（语义偏移：层级升到总科，范围放宽）
homo + -inae（亚科词尾）→ 人亚科的（语义偏移：指人亚科，含大猿与人类）
humanus（homo 的形容词）→ 人的；人
hominid + like（相似）→ 类似人科的（语义偏移：用于描述特征而非归类）

senses.title: A member of the family Hominidae
senses.titleCN: 现代分类：人科（含大猿与人类）的成员
senses.definition: any member of the family Hominidae in its modern sense, including great apes and humans
senses.definitionCN: 现代意义上的科级分类上的人科成员，包括大猿与人类
senses.example: The ape in the next case is, strictly speaking, also a hominid.
senses.exampleCN: 严格说来，隔壁展柜里的那只猿也是人科成员。
senses.why: The suffix -idae marks a zoological family, and the family now holds gorillas, chimpanzees, humans and their fossil relatives; the word therefore covers more than most readers expect.
senses.whyCN: -idae 是动物学上的科级词尾，而这个科如今包含大猩猩、黑猩猩、人类及其化石亲属；因此这个词覆盖的范围比多数读者预想的大。

senses.title: The human line only, in older usage
senses.titleCN: 旧义：仅指人类这一支及其近亲
senses.definition: in older literature, a member of the human family only, excluding the other great apes
senses.definitionCN: 旧文献中仅指人类这一支的成员，不含其他大猿
senses.example: Older papers use hominid where a modern author would write hominin.
senses.exampleCN: 旧论文用 hominid 的地方，现代作者会写 hominin。
senses.why: When Hominidae meant only humans and their extinct relatives, the word was narrower; taxonomy changed and the word did not, so both senses circulate in the literature.
senses.whyCN: 当 Hominidae 只指人类及其已灭绝亲属时，这个词更窄；分类变了而词没变，于是两种义在文献里同时流通。

senses.title: A fossil specimen
senses.titleCN: 化石标本：博物馆或论文里的一个个体
senses.definition: a particular fossil individual assigned to that family
senses.definitionCN: 被归入该科的某一具体化石个体
senses.example: The hominid pelvis in the drawer had been mislabelled for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 抽屉里这块人科骨盆被错标了三十年。
senses.why: Specimens are what fill drawers and catalogues, so the noun shifted from a class to a counted thing; a label on a bone says hominid in the same way it says femur.
senses.whyCN: 标本才是抽屉与目录里的实物，因此名词从一类变成可数的一件；骨头上写 hominid，与写 femur 是同一种用法。

senses.title: A descriptive adjective
senses.titleCN: 描述性形容词：具人科特征的
senses.definition: having the anatomical features associated with the family
senses.definitionCN: 具有该科解剖特征的
senses.example: The hominid jaw was deep and the teeth were large.
senses.exampleCN: 这块人科下颌很深，牙齿很大。
senses.why: English lets many taxonomic nouns double as adjectives; here the adjective means 'shaped like a member of this family', which is looser than the classification itself.
senses.whyCN: 英语里许多分类名词可兼作形容词；此处形容词意为「形状像该科成员」，比分类本身更宽松。

senses.title: Popular 'early human ancestor'
senses.titleCN: 通俗用法：早期人类祖先
senses.definition: in popular writing, any early ancestor of modern humans
senses.definitionCN: 通俗写作中现代人类的任何早期祖先
senses.example: The documentary called every fossil ape a hominid and every one of them our grandfather.
senses.exampleCN: 纪录片把每块化石猿都称作人科动物，把每一块都说成我们的祖父。
senses.why: Popular writing needs a short word for 'old human relative', and hominid was available; the loose sense then spread through museums and film.
senses.whyCN: 通俗写作需要一个短词来说「古老的人类亲戚」，hominid 正好可用；这个宽松义随后经博物馆与影片扩散。

senses.title: The taxonomic rank label
senses.titleCN: 分类层级标签：科这一级的名称
senses.definition: the family-level category itself, as used in classification
senses.definitionCN: 分类学中「科」这一级所用的名称
senses.example: The label on the case reads Hominidae, of which hominid is the everyday form.
senses.exampleCN: 展柜上的标签写着 Hominidae，hominid 是它的日常说法。
senses.why: The noun is a back-formation from the family name: -idae belongs to the taxon, -id to one member of it, a pattern repeated across zoology.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是从科名反向构成的：-idae 属于分类单元，-id 属于其中一个成员，这一模式在动物学中反复出现。

senses.title: A comparative-anatomy reference
senses.titleCN: 比较解剖学的参照：用来对照的骨架
senses.definition: a reference specimen in comparative anatomy, as in a hominid skeleton
senses.definitionCN: 比较解剖学中作对照的标本，如人科骨架
senses.example: Students compare a hominid skeleton with a chimpanzee's on the same bench.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们在同一张台子上把人科骨架与黑猩猩骨架对照。
senses.why: Anatomy teaches by comparison, and the word became a convenient label for one side of the comparison, independent of any claim about ancestry.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学靠比较来教，这个词于是成了比较中一侧的方便标签，与任何关于祖先的主张无关。

senses.title: An evolutionary grade
senses.titleCN: 演化等级：以「人科水平」描述形态阶段
senses.definition: a grade of organisation rather than a strictly defined family, as in hominid-grade
senses.definitionCN: 指形态组织的一种水平，而非严格界定的科，如 hominid-grade
senses.example: Some writers speak of hominid-grade posture without committing to a family.
senses.exampleCN: 有些作者说有「人科水平」的体态，却不对科属表态。
senses.why: Grade and clade are different ideas: a grade describes a level of adaptation, which lets hominid be used for a body plan rather than a branch.
senses.whyCN: 等级与支系是两回事：等级描述适应水平，于是 hominid 可用来指一套身体方案，而不是一个分支。

intro.en: Hominid is a nineteenth-century taxonomic formation from the Latin stem for 'person' plus a family ending; the family ending is clear, the stem's deeper origin is not.
intro.cn: hominid 是 19 世纪从拉丁「人」词干加科级词尾构成的分类学术语；词尾清楚，词干的更深来源则不然。

items.en: Homo, hominis meant 'human being'. Its deeper origin is disputed; a connection with humus 'earth' would give 'earthling', but that is a hypothesis and not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: homo, hominis 意为「人」。其更深来源有争议；与 humus「土地」联系可得出「地上之人」，但这只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Nineteenth-century zoologists formed family names on Latin stems with the ending -idae, and Hominidae was coined for the family containing humans.
items.cn: 19 世纪动物学者用拉丁词干加 -idae 构成科名，Hominidae 即为人所在的科所造。

items.en: English took the family name and made a singular noun hominid for one member, with the adjective following immediately.
items.cn: 英语取用科名，造出单数名词 hominid 指一个成员，形容词用法随即跟上。

items.en: From the late twentieth century comparative genetics placed gorillas and chimpanzees inside the same family, so Hominidae widened and hominid with it.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期比较遗传学把大猩猩与黑猩猩放进同一个科，Hominidae 因此变宽，hominid 也随之变宽。

items.en: Older textbooks and museum labels still use the pre-reclassification sense, so the word has two live readings that differ by a whole family.
items.cn: 旧教科书与博物馆标签仍用重新分类之前的义，因此这个词有两种并行的读法，相差整整一个科。

items.en: Source uncertain: the taxonomic date is approximate for the English noun, and the pre-Latin origin of homo is unknown, with all proposed forms reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语名词的确切分类年代只有约数；homo 在拉丁语之前的来源不明，所拟形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the taxonomic words one rank away from hominid, which are the usual source of error; group two holds the everyday relatives.
note.cn: 第一组是与 hominid 相差一个分类层级的词，也是错误的常见来源；第二组是日常说法中的亲属词。

entries.definition: A member of the tribe Hominini, the human line after the split from chimpanzees; narrower than hominid and now preferred for fossils on that line.
entries.definitionCN: 人族成员，指与黑猩猩分开之后的人类这一支；比 hominid 窄，今多用于该支的化石。

entries.definition: A member of the superfamily Hominoidea, which adds the great apes to the picture; broader than hominid.
entries.definitionCN: 人形总科成员，把大猿也算进来；比 hominid 宽。

entries.definition: A member of the subfamily Homininae, the African apes and humans together; a rank between family and tribe.
entries.definitionCN: 人亚科成员，即非洲猿与人类；层级在科与族之间。

entries.definition: A member of Homo sapiens only, with no fossil relatives included.
entries.definitionCN: 仅指智人这一物种，不含化石亲属。

entries.definition: A member of the order Primates, which contains hominids among many others.
entries.definitionCN: 灵长目成员，人科只是其中一支。

entries.definition: A gorilla, chimpanzee, orangutan or human, in plain language; the same set as modern Hominidae.
entries.definitionCN: 日常语言中的大猩猩、黑猩猩、猩猩或人；与现代 Hominidae 同一集合。

entries.definition: Any earlier population from which a later one descends; it makes no taxonomic claim.
entries.definitionCN: 后代所出自的任何较早群体；不作分类学断言。

entries.definition: An animal that walks on two legs; several hominids are bipeds, but the words are not equivalent.
entries.definitionCN: 两足行走的动物；若干人科动物是两足，但两词并不等同。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real ranks and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实词尾、真实分类层级与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: -idae marks a family, -id marks one member of it; the same pattern runs through zoology.
normal.cn: -idae 标记科，-id 标记其中一个成员；动物学中同一模式反复出现。

normal.en: The family now includes the great apes, so a gorilla is a hominid even though it is not a human ancestor.
normal.cn: 这个科如今包含大猿，因此大猩猩是人科成员，尽管它不是人类祖先。

normal.en: The family runs Hominidae, hominid, hominin, hominoid, hominine, human.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 Hominidae、hominid、hominin、hominoid、hominine、human。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: early hominid, hominid fossils, hominid evolution.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：早期人科动物、人科化石、人科演化。

normal.en: Older texts use the narrow sense; modern texts use the wide sense; ask which family the author means.
normal.cn: 旧文用窄义，现代文用宽义；要问作者指的是哪个科。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer where a pelvis and a femur are introduced to each other after thirty years apart.
abstract.cn: 想象抽屉里一块骨盆与一根股骨，分离三十年后才被介绍相识。

abstract.en: Picture a family photograph in which the cousins keep being cropped out and then restored.
abstract.cn: 想象一张全家福，表亲们先被裁掉，后来又被放回。

abstract.en: Picture a label that is one rank too low for the bone it describes.
abstract.cn: 想象一张标签，比它所描述的骨头低了整整一级。

examples.en: The hominid fossil was reassigned to a different genus after the jaw was cleaned.
examples.cn: 下颌清理之后，这块人科化石被改归另一个属。

examples.en: Every hominid in the case shares a shoulder built for climbing.
examples.cn: 展柜里每一具人科骨架都有为攀爬而生的肩。

examples.en: The word hominid now covers the apes too, which surprises many visitors.
examples.cn: hominid 如今也涵盖猿类，这让许多参观者意外。

dict_mnemonic.text: homin（人）+ id（科成员）＝ 人科的成员；记「层级三件套：hominoid 总科、hominid 科、hominin 族」。

root: 新拉丁 Hominidae：拉丁 homo（homin-「人」）+ -idae（科级分类词尾）；homo 更深来源不确定，与 humus「土地」的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one taxonomic word as its family grew: the modern wide family, the older narrow one, a counted fossil, a descriptive adjective, a popular ancestor, the rank label, an anatomical reference and an evolutionary grade.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着一个分类词随其科的范围扩大：现代宽义、旧日窄义、可数的化石、描述性形容词、通俗的祖先义、层级标签、解剖参照，以及演化等级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pelvis and a femur joined in a drawer under a label that names a rank, not a bone.
core.cn: 核心意象：抽屉里拼在一起的骨盆与股骨，标签写的是分类层级，而不是骨名。

branches.en: TWO WIDTHS OF ONE FAMILY: the modern reading that admits apes, and the older one that excluded them.
branches.cn: 同一个科的两种宽度：含猿的现代读法，与排除猿的旧读法。

branches.en: FROM CLASS TO OBJECT: a counted fossil in a drawer, and a skeleton used for comparison.
branches.cn: 从类到物：抽屉里可数的化石，与用作对照的骨架。

branches.en: DESCRIPTION AND STORY: the adjective for features, and the museum word for an ancestor.
branches.cn: 描述与故事：指特征的形容词，与博物馆里指祖先的词。

branches.en: THE RANK ITSELF: a family name turned back into a noun for its members.
branches.cn: 层级本身：科名反向构成指其成员的名词。

branches.en: THE LOOSER IDEA: a level of adaptation rather than a branch of the tree.
branches.cn: 更松的概念：一种适应水平，而非树上的一支。

intro.en: The word is a taxonomic suffix on a Latin stem, and the same stem with different rank endings produces the words most often confused with it.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁词干加分类学词尾，同一词干换不同层级词尾，就产生最易与它混淆的几个词。

latinIntro.en: Latin homo supplies the stem homin-; the endings -idae, -ini, -inae and -oidea mark family, tribe, subfamily and superfamily, and English adds -id for a single member.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 homo 提供词干 homin-；-idae、-ini、-inae、-oidea 分别标记科、族、亚科、总科，英语再加 -id 指单个成员。

items.example: The stem is shared by every rank name in the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干为这一族的各层级名称共用。

items.structure: New Latin family ending from Greek -idai
items.example: The ending marks the rank that contains genera.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾标记包含属的那一级。

items.example: The word names one member, not the family itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词指一个成员，而非科本身。

items.example: The same stem with a tribe ending gives hominin.
items.exampleCN: 同一词干换族级词尾即成 hominin。

items.example: The same stem with a subfamily ending gives hominine.
items.exampleCN: 同一词干换亚科词尾即成 hominine。

items.example: The same stem with a superfamily ending gives hominoid.
items.exampleCN: 同一词干换总科词尾即成 hominoid。

items.example: The family name is capitalized and italicized in zoology.
items.exampleCN: 科名在动物学中大写并用斜体。

items.example: The narrower word is now standard for the human line.
items.exampleCN: 较窄的这个词如今是人类这一支的标准称谓。

items.example: The wider word includes the apes.
items.exampleCN: 较宽的这个词包含猿类。

definition_zh: 人族成员；人类这一支（与黑猩猩分化后）的物种
definition_en: a member of the tribe Hominini, the human lineage after its split from the chimpanzee line
core_image: 两条岔开的足迹：一条通向树，一条通向地面，后一条上还叠着更小的脚印
scene: 下层位出土的牙齿被送去测量，报告上只写了族名，没有写属名。The hominin teeth from the lower layer were smaller than anyone had expected.
sceneCN: 这里「人族成员」指人类这一支的一个物种（第 1 个义项：人族成员）；句意为下层位出土的人族牙齿比任何人预想的都小。

pos.zh: 人族成员（可数，复数 hominins）

derivatives.zh: 拉丁 homo（人）+ -ini（族级分类词尾）→ 人族（分类学上的族名）
拉丁 homo + -idae（科级词尾）→ 人科成员（语义偏移：层级更高，范围更宽）
