senses.title: A member of the tribe Hominini
senses.titleCN: 人族成员：与黑猩猩分化后的人类这一支
senses.definition: a member of the tribe Hominini, the lineage that split from the chimpanzee line
senses.definitionCN: 与黑猩猩一支分化之后的人类谱系成员
senses.example: The hominin teeth from the lower layer were smaller than anyone had expected.
senses.exampleCN: 下层位出土的人族牙齿比任何人预想的都小。
senses.why: The ending -ini marks a tribe, one rank below family; because that tribe was drawn to hold humans and their extinct relatives after the split, the word names a branch rather than a body plan.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ini 标记族，比科低一级；这一族被划定来容纳分化之后的人类及其已灭绝亲属，因此这个词命名的是一个分支，而非一套身体方案。

senses.title: A fossil species on that branch
senses.titleCN: 该支上的化石物种：一个具体物种
senses.definition: a particular extinct species assigned to that branch
senses.definitionCN: 被归入这一支的某一已灭绝物种
senses.example: Each hominin in the collection has been dated by the ash above it.
senses.exampleCN: 藏品中每一个人族物种都是靠其上方的火山灰定年的。
senses.why: A branch is abstract; a species is something you can hold. The noun therefore also names the units that fill museum drawers.
senses.whyCN: 分支是抽象的，物种却能拿在手里；因此这个名词也指填满博物馆抽屉的那些单位。

senses.title: A descriptive adjective
senses.titleCN: 描述性形容词：具人族特征的
senses.definition: showing the traits associated with that branch
senses.definitionCN: 具有该支特征的
senses.example: The hominin foot had an arch, which settled the argument about shoes.
senses.exampleCN: 这只人族足部有足弓，平息了关于鞋的争论。
senses.why: As with hominid, the noun doubles as an adjective; here the adjective signals traits taken to mark the branch, such as an arched foot or a flat face.
senses.whyCN: 与 hominid 一样，这个名词兼作形容词；此处形容词表示被认为标记该支的特征，如足弓或扁平的脸。

senses.title: The precise alternative to hominid
senses.titleCN: 对比 hominid 的精确用法：强调层级更窄
senses.definition: the taxonomic term preferred when the narrower branch must be distinguished from the wider family
senses.definitionCN: 需要把较窄的分支与较宽的科区分开时所用的术语
senses.example: The authors write hominin precisely to exclude the gorilla from the sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 作者写 hominin 正是为了把大猩猩排除在句子之外。
senses.why: Because hominid widened to include the apes, a narrower word was needed for the human branch; hominin supplied it, and the contrast is now a marker of careful writing.
senses.whyCN: 由于 hominid 变宽而包含猿类，就需要一个更窄的词来指人类这一支；hominin 补上这个位置，如今这组对照成了用词谨慎的标志。

senses.title: Popular 'early hominin'
senses.titleCN: 通俗用法：早期人族成员
senses.definition: in popular science, any early member of the human branch
senses.definitionCN: 通俗科学中人类这一支的任何早期成员
senses.example: The article called every early hominin a candidate for our ancestor.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章把每一种早期人族成员都称作我们祖先的候选。
senses.why: Popular writing adopted the technical word because it sounds precise and fits a headline; the popular sense is looser than the taxonomic one.
senses.whyCN: 通俗写作采用这个术语，因为它听起来精确又适合标题；通俗义比分类学义宽松。

senses.title: A point on the evolutionary timeline
senses.titleCN: 时间线上的一个节点：谱系图上的位置
senses.definition: a named point or segment on the branching diagram of human ancestry
senses.definitionCN: 人类祖先分叉图上的一个命名节点或段落
senses.example: The chart lists five hominins between the first stone tools and the first hearths.
senses.exampleCN: 图表在最早的石器与最早的灶之间列了五种人族成员。
senses.why: Timelines need countable labels for segments; the noun supplies them, and a chart can then be read left to right.
senses.whyCN: 时间线需要可数的段标，这个名词正好提供；图表于是可以从左读到右。

senses.title: A unit of the fossil record
senses.titleCN: 化石记录的单位：可比较的一批标本
senses.definition: a comparative unit of the fossil record, often a named sample
senses.definitionCN: 化石记录中的比较单位，常是一个命名样本
senses.example: The hominin sample from the cave is too small to settle the question.
senses.exampleCN: 这个洞穴的人族样本太小，回答不了这个问题。
senses.why: In practice specimens are grouped into samples before any statistic is run, and the noun is used for those groups as well as for the species.
senses.whyCN: 实际上，任何统计之前都要把标本归成样本，而这个名词也用来指这些组，而不只是物种。

senses.title: Evidence in a taxonomic dispute
senses.titleCN: 分类争议中的证据：用来主张拆分或合并
senses.definition: a category whose boundaries are argued over in debates about splitting and lumping
senses.definitionCN: 在「拆」与「并」之争中被争论边界的类别
senses.example: Whether that jaw is a hominin at all is the whole dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 那块下颌到底算不算人族成员，正是整场争议。
senses.why: Where a rank is drawn is a decision, not a discovery; naming a fossil a hominin is therefore a claim that can be contested, and the word carries that argument inside it.
senses.whyCN: 层级画在哪里是决定，而非发现；把一块化石称作 hominin 因此是一个可被反驳的主张，这个词本身带着这场争论。

intro.en: Hominin is the newest of the family words, formed when twentieth-century taxonomy needed a rank narrower than the family; its stem is the old Latin word for a person.
intro.cn: hominin 是这一族词里最新的一个，形成于 20 世纪分类学需要一个比科更窄的层级之时；其词干仍是古老的拉丁语「人」。

items.en: Homo, hominis meant 'human being'; its deeper origin is disputed, and the humus 'earth' connection is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: homo, hominis 意为「人」；更深来源有争议，与 humus「土地」的联系是假说而非已证实的派生。

items.en: The family name Hominidae was already established in the nineteenth century, built on the same stem with the family ending.
items.cn: 科名 Hominidae 在 19 世纪已确立，用同一词干加科级词尾构成。

items.en: When comparative genetics placed the great apes inside the family, the older word hominid no longer marked the human branch alone.
items.cn: 当比较遗传学把大猿放进这个科，旧的 hominid 便不再单独标记人类这一支。

items.en: Taxonomists drew a tribe inside the subfamily to hold humans and their extinct relatives after the chimpanzee split, and named it Hominini with the tribe ending -ini.
items.cn: 分类学者在人亚科内划出一个族，容纳黑猩猩分化后的人类及其已灭绝亲属，并以族级词尾 -ini 命名为 Hominini。

items.en: English formed hominin from the tribe name in the later twentieth century; it spread quickly because museum labels needed a short precise word.
items.cn: 英语在 20 世纪后期由族名构成 hominin；它传播很快，因为博物馆标签需要一个简短精确的词。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English use is dated only approximately, and the pre-Latin origin of homo remains unknown, so proposed forms are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语首见年代只有约数；homo 在拉丁语之前的来源仍不明，所拟形式均为重构。

note.en: Group one holds the rank words that differ only by their endings; group two holds the wider categories a hominin also belongs to.
note.cn: 第一组是仅靠词尾区分的层级词；第二组是人族成员同时所属的更宽类别。

entries.definition: A member of the family Hominidae, which now includes the great apes; correct but less precise for the human branch.
entries.definitionCN: 人科成员，今含大猿；说法正确，但指人类这一支时不够精确。

entries.definition: A member of the subfamily Homininae, the African apes and humans together.
entries.definitionCN: 人亚科成员，即非洲猿与人类。

entries.definition: A member of the superfamily Hominoidea, the widest of these categories.
entries.definitionCN: 人形总科成员，是这些类别中最宽的。

entries.definition: A member of Homo sapiens, the only surviving hominin.
entries.definitionCN: 智人成员，是唯一存续至今的人族成员。

entries.definition: A member of the genus Australopithecus and its allies, early hominins with small brains.
entries.definitionCN: 南方古猿属及其近亲的成员，是脑量小的早期人族。

entries.definition: A member of Homo neanderthalensis, a hominin that interbred with modern humans.
entries.definitionCN: 尼安德特人，曾与现代人杂交的人族成员。

entries.definition: A member of the order Primates, which contains the hominins among many others.
entries.definitionCN: 灵长目成员，人族只是其中一支。

entries.definition: An earlier population from which a later one descends; the word makes no claim about tribe or family.
entries.definitionCN: 后代所出自的较早群体；该词不对族或科作断言。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real rank endings, real fossil names and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的层级词尾、真实化石名与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: -ini is the tribe ending, so hominin is one rank narrower than hominid and one wider than a species.
normal.cn: -ini 是族级词尾，因此 hominin 比 hominid 窄一级，比物种宽一级。

normal.en: The tribe was drawn to hold the human branch after the chimpanzee split, so the word names a branch, not a shape.
normal.cn: 这个族是为容纳黑猩猩分化后的人类一支而划的，因此这个词命名分支，而非形状。

normal.en: The family runs Hominini, hominin, hominid, hominine, hominoid, australopithecine.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 Hominini、hominin、hominid、hominine、hominoid、australopithecine。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: early hominin, hominin fossils, the hominin lineage.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：早期人族成员、人族化石、人族谱系。

normal.en: In a sentence about ancestry, hominin keeps the gorilla out; hominid lets it in.
normal.cn: 在谈祖先的句子里，hominin 把大猩猩挡在外面，hominid 则放它进来。

abstract.en: Picture two footprints diverging, one toward trees and one toward open ground.
abstract.cn: 想象两串脚印分开，一串通向树，一串通向开阔地。

abstract.en: Picture a label so precise that it excludes a cousin standing beside the case.
abstract.cn: 想象一张精确到把展柜旁的堂亲排除在外的标签。

abstract.en: Picture a chart whose left edge changes every time a new jaw is found.
abstract.cn: 想象一张图表，每找到一块新下颌，左端就要改一次。

examples.en: The hominin lineage lost a robust jaw before it gained a large brain.
examples.cn: 人族谱系先失去粗壮的下颌，之后才得到大容量的脑。

examples.en: Museum labels were rewritten from hominid to hominin after the taxonomy changed.
examples.cn: 分类改变之后，博物馆标签从 hominid 改写为 hominin。

examples.en: A single hominin tooth can support two incompatible reconstructions.
examples.cn: 一颗人族牙齿可以同时支持两套互不相容的重建。

dict_mnemonic.text: homin（人）+ in（族级词尾）＝ 人族成员；记「比科窄一级，比种宽一级」。

root: 新拉丁 Hominini：拉丁 homo（homin-「人」）+ -ini（族级分类词尾）；homo 更深来源不确定，与 humus「土地」的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses narrow one word from a tribe to a tooth: the branch member, a fossil species, an adjective, the precise alternative to hominid, the popular ancestor, a point on a chart, a sample in the record, and a claim in a taxonomic dispute.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个词从族缩到一颗牙：分支成员、化石物种、形容词、hominid 的精确替代、通俗祖先、图表节点、记录中的样本，以及分类争议中的主张。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two sets of footprints splitting, with smaller prints laid over the one that leads to open ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：两串分开的脚印，通向开阔地的那一串上叠着更小的脚印。

branches.en: BRANCH AND UNIT: the tribe as a whole, then the countable species that fills it.
branches.cn: 分支与单位：先是整个族，再是填满它的可数物种。

branches.en: SHAPE AND PRECISION: an adjective for traits, and a term chosen to keep the apes out.
branches.cn: 形状与精确：指特征的形容词，以及为把猿挡在外面而选的术语。

branches.en: STORY AND CHART: the headline ancestor, and the labelled point on a timeline.
branches.cn: 故事与图表：标题里的祖先，与时间线上带标签的一点。

branches.en: THE SAMPLE: specimens grouped before any number is calculated.
branches.cn: 样本：任何计算之前先归好的标本组。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT: where a rank is drawn is a decision that can be contested.
branches.cn: 争论：层级画在哪里是一个可被反驳的决定。

intro.en: Hominin is the same Latin stem as hominid with a different rank ending, and the endings are what separate the four commonly confused words.
intro.cn: hominin 与 hominid 共用同一拉丁词干，只是层级词尾不同，而词尾正是区分四个易混词的关键。

latinIntro.en: Latin homo supplies homin-; New Latin endings mark the ranks, -idae family, -inae subfamily, -ini tribe and -oidea superfamily, and English adds -in for a member of the tribe.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 homo 提供 homin-；新拉丁词尾标记层级：-idae 科、-inae 亚科、-ini 族、-oidea 总科，英语再加 -in 指该族成员。

items.example: The stem is shared with every rank name in this family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干与本族各层级名称共用。

items.example: The ending is the only thing that separates hominin from hominid.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾是 hominin 与 hominid 的唯一区别。

items.example: The word names the narrowest rank in common use.
items.exampleCN: 这个词指日常使用中最窄的层级。

items.example: The wider word now admits the great apes.
items.exampleCN: 较宽的这个词如今容纳大猿。

items.example: The intermediate word names the African apes and humans together.
items.exampleCN: 中间这个词指非洲猿与人类的合集。

items.example: The widest word takes in all the apes.
items.exampleCN: 最宽的这个词包含所有猿类。

items.example: The tribe name is capitalized and italicized.
items.exampleCN: 族名大写并用斜体。

items.example: The compound names an early part of the tribe.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词命名族中较早的一支。

items.structure: Neanderthal, a German valley, + -ensis in the scientific name
items.example: The place name became a species name and then a common noun.
items.exampleCN: 地名先成为种名，再成为普通名词。

latinEntries.structure: Hominini (New Latin, f. plural, tribe rank)
latinEntries.meaning: the tribe of humans and their extinct relatives
latinEntries.meaningCN: 人类及其已灭绝亲属的族

definition_zh: 灵长类动物；灵长目成员；（宗教）首席主教
definition_en: a mammal of the order Primates, or a senior bishop in some churches
core_image: 一只向前看的眼睛、一只能对握的手，再加一条能缠住树枝的尾巴
scene: 动物园的说明牌上画着一只对握的手和一双朝前的眼睛，参观者伸手比了比。A primate is defined less by its thumb than by the eyes it aims at the next branch.
sceneCN: 这里「灵长类动物」指灵长目的一个成员（第 1 个义项：动物学上的目成员）；句意为灵长类与其说由拇指界定，不如说由那双瞄准下一根树枝的眼睛界定。

pos.zh: 灵长类动物；灵长目成员（可数，复数 primates）
首席主教；教省主教（部分教会用语，读音常作 /ˈpraɪmət/）

derivatives.zh: 拉丁 primas「居首者」→ 灵长目（林奈所定的目名，取「首位」之意）
primate + -logy（希腊「学问」）→ 灵长类学
primatology + -ist → 灵长类学家
primacy + -al（关系形容词后缀）→ 首席主教的；首席的（语义偏移：指教会职权）
primus「第一」+ -acy（状态名词后缀）→ 首位；首要地位
primus + -al → 最初的；原始的（语义偏移：从「第一」到「最早」）
primarius「第一等的」→ 初级读本；底漆（语义偏移：起先导作用之物）

senses.title: A member of the order Primates
senses.titleCN: 灵长目成员：动物学上的一个目
senses.definition: a mammal belonging to the order Primates, with grasping hands and forward-facing eyes
senses.definitionCN: 具有抓握的手与朝前双眼的灵长目哺乳动物
senses.example: A primate is defined less by its thumb than by the eyes it aims at the next branch.
senses.exampleCN: 灵长类与其说由拇指界定，不如说由那双瞄准下一根树枝的眼睛界定。
senses.why: Latin primas meant 'of first rank'; Linnaeus gave the order that name, and the word has named its members ever since, with grasping and vision as the usual diagnostic traits.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 primas 意为「居首的」；林奈给这个目取了这个名字，此后这个词便指其成员，抓握与视觉是常用辨识特征。

senses.title: An animal used in research
senses.titleCN: 实验动物：被用于研究的灵长类个体
senses.definition: an individual primate kept or studied in a laboratory setting
senses.definitionCN: 在实验室环境中被饲养或研究的灵长类个体
senses.example: The primate in the cognition study had been trained on touchscreens for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这项认知研究里的灵长类个体已在触摸屏上训练多年。
senses.why: Because primates are close relatives, they became the standard animal for questions about cognition and disease; the noun then names a research subject as much as a taxon.
senses.whyCN: 由于灵长类与人类亲缘近，它们成了认知与疾病问题的标准实验动物；于是这个名词既指分类单元，也指研究对象。

senses.title: A species in an ecosystem
senses.titleCN: 生态中的物种：作为群落一员
senses.definition: a primate species considered as part of an ecological community
senses.definitionCN: 被当作生态群落一员的灵长类物种
senses.example: Every primate in the canopy disperses seeds for the trees that feed it.
senses.exampleCN: 树冠层里的每一种灵长类都在为供养它的树木传播种子。
senses.why: Ecology counts species rather than specimens, so the word shifts to the population level: a primate here means one node in a food web.
senses.whyCN: 生态学数的是物种而非标本，因此这个词转到种群层面：此处的 primate 指食物网中的一个节点。

senses.title: A relative in plain speech
senses.titleCN: 通俗说法：我们的灵长类近亲
senses.definition: an informal way of calling monkeys and apes our close relatives
senses.definitionCN: 把猴与猿称作我们近亲的口语说法
senses.example: The film kept saying that every primate shares most of our genes.
senses.exampleCN: 影片反复说每一种灵长类都与我们共享大部分基因。
senses.why: Plain speech uses the taxonomic word for kinship rather than classification; the tone is warm, and the precision is deliberately loose.
senses.whyCN: 口语用这个分类词谈亲缘而非分类；语气亲切，精确度则有意放宽。

senses.title: A senior bishop
senses.titleCN: 首席主教：某些教会中的教省主教
senses.definition: a bishop holding the highest office in a province or national church
senses.definitionCN: 在教省或全国教会中居最高职位的 bishop
senses.example: The primate of the province presided at the consecration.
senses.exampleCN: 该教省的首席主教主持了祝圣礼。
senses.why: This sense is older in English than the zoological one: Latin primas named a church officer of the first rank, and the ecclesiastical word entered English through French.
senses.whyCN: 这一义在英语中比动物学义更早：拉丁 primas 指居首的教会职务，教会用语经法语进入英语。

senses.title: An attributive label
senses.titleCN: 定语用法：用于研究领域或器官
senses.definition: used before a noun to mark the field or the organ, as in primate cognition
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前、标记研究领域或器官，如灵长类认知
senses.example: Primate brains are studied for the same reason their hands are.
senses.exampleCN: 研究灵长类的脑，与研究它们的手出于同一理由。
senses.why: Taxonomic nouns regularly become modifiers in English; the attributive use says which order the study or organ belongs to, without naming an individual.
senses.whyCN: 分类名词在英语中经常作修饰语；定语用法说明研究或器官属于哪个目，而不指名个体。

senses.title: The order as a category
senses.titleCN: 作为分类范畴：目这一级
senses.definition: the order itself as a taxonomic category
senses.definitionCN: 分类学上「目」这一级本身
senses.example: Primates is the order; primate is the member, and the two are not interchangeable.
senses.exampleCN: Primates 是目，primate 是成员，两者不可互换。
senses.why: A category and its members share a stem but not a grammatical number: one is a capitalized plural taxon, the other a countable noun.
senses.whyCN: 范畴与其成员共享词干，但数不同：一个是首字母大写的复数分类名，一个是可数名词。

senses.title: Popular use for monkeys and apes
senses.titleCN: 通俗泛指：猴与猿的统称
senses.definition: in everyday use, any monkey or ape, with no taxonomic care
senses.definitionCN: 日常使用中泛指任何猴或猿，不计分类
senses.example: The sign said primates, and the children looked for the monkeys first.
senses.exampleCN: 牌子上写着灵长类，孩子们先去找猴子。
senses.why: Popular usage keeps the word but drops the boundaries; the result is a broad everyday sense that a specialist would not use in writing.
senses.whyCN: 通俗用法保留词形却不管边界；结果是一个专家不会在写作中使用的宽泛日常义。

senses.title: A grade in evolution
senses.titleCN: 演化等级：以灵长类水平描述适应
senses.definition: a level of adaptation described as primate-grade, rather than a formal taxon
senses.definitionCN: 以「灵长类水平」描述的适应等级，而非正式分类单元
senses.example: Some early mammals are described as primate-like without being placed in the order.
senses.exampleCN: 有些早期哺乳动物被描述为「似灵长类」，却没有被归入该目。
senses.why: Grade thinking lets writers use a taxon's name for a body plan that appeared before the taxon did, which is why primate-like exists beside primate.
senses.whyCN: 等级思维让作者用一个分类名来指在该分类出现之前就有的身体方案，这就是 primate-like 与 primate 并存的原因。

intro.en: Primate has two histories that meet in one spelling: a church office of the first rank, and an order of mammals named by Linnaeus. Both go back to the Latin word for 'first'.
intro.cn: primate 的两段历史汇于一种拼写：居首的教会职务，以及林奈命名的哺乳动物目。两者都回到拉丁语的「第一」。

items.en: Primus 'first' is a fully attested Latin ordinal with a clear Indo-European background; unlike many words in this batch, its Latin form is not in doubt.
items.cn: primus「第一」是书证充分的拉丁序数词，印欧背景清楚；与本批许多词不同，其拉丁形式并无争议。

items.en: Primas, primatis meant 'one of the first rank, chief'; it was used of leading men and later of leading bishops.
items.cn: primas, primatis 意为「居首者、首领」；先用于显要人物，后用于首席主教。

items.en: English primate entered through Old French primat in the medieval period, meaning a bishop of the highest rank in a province.
items.cn: 英语 primate 于中世纪经古法语 primat 进入，指教省中职位最高的主教。

items.en: Linnaeus placed humans and apes in one order and called it Primates, 'the first ones'; he did not publish a detailed reason, so the motive behind the name is inferred rather than documented.
items.cn: 林奈把人与猿放进同一个目，取名 Primates，意为「居首者」；他没有发表详细理由，因此命名动机是推断而非有据。

items.en: The order later expanded to include lemurs and other groups, while the church sense continued separately in ecclesiastical English.
items.cn: 这个目后来扩展到包含狐猴等类群，而教会义在教会英语中另行延续。

items.en: Source uncertain (naming motive): Linnaeus's reason for choosing Primates is not established, and explanations offered for it are interpretations; the date 1758 is that of the tenth edition.
items.cn: 来源不确定（命名动机）：林奈选用 Primates 的理由没有定论，各种解释均属推测；1758 年指《自然系统》第十版之年。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same 'first' stem, which are the commonest look-alike errors; group two holds the wider and narrower animal categories.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「第一」词干、最常被看错的词；第二组是更宽与更窄的动物类别。

entries.definition: The state of being first in rank; it shares the stem but names a position, not an animal.
entries.definitionCN: 居首的状态；共享词干，但指位置，不指动物。

entries.definition: Belonging to the earliest stage; the sense moved from 'first in rank' to 'first in time'.
entries.definitionCN: 属于最早阶段的；词义从「位次第一」转到「时间最早」。

entries.definition: From primarius 'of the first class': an introductory book or a first coat of paint.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 primarius「第一等的」：入门书或第一道漆。

entries.definition: The capitalized plural is the order's name; the singular is one member of it.
entries.definitionCN: 首字母大写的复数是目名；单数指其中一个成员。

entries.definition: Any warm-blooded vertebrate that feeds its young; primates are one order within it.
entries.definitionCN: 任何哺乳幼崽的恒温脊椎动物；灵长目只是其中一个目。

entries.definition: The tailless large primates, gorillas, chimpanzees, orangutans and humans; narrower than primate.
entries.definitionCN: 无尾的大型灵长类，即大猩猩、黑猩猩、猩猩与人；比 primate 窄。

entries.definition: Most non-ape primates, usually with tails; the everyday word children reach for first.
entries.definitionCN: 多数非猿的灵长类，通常有尾；孩子最先想到的日常词。

entries.definition: A member of the family containing great apes and humans, one branch of the primates.
entries.definitionCN: 含大猿与人类的那个科的成员，是灵长类中的一支。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin layers, real ranks and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁层次、真实层级与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Primas 'of the first rank' gives both the church officer and Linnaeus's order of 'the first ones'.
normal.cn: primas「居首的」既给出教会职务，也给出林奈那个「居首者」的目。

normal.en: Grasping hands and forward-facing eyes are the usual diagnostic pair.
normal.cn: 抓握的手与朝前的双眼是常用的辨识配对。

normal.en: The family runs primate, primates, Primates, primatology, primatologist, primacy, primal.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 primate、primates、Primates、primatology、primatologist、primacy、primal。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: primate species, primate behaviour, the primate order.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：灵长类物种、灵长类行为、灵长目。

normal.en: Mind the number: Primates is the order, a primate is one of its members.
normal.cn: 注意数：首字母大写的复数是目名，单数形式才是其中一个成员。

abstract.en: Picture an eye that looks forward and a hand that can hold what the eye has chosen.
abstract.cn: 想象一只朝前看的眼，与一只拿得住眼睛所选之物的手。

abstract.en: Picture a bishop and a lemur sharing one word without ever meeting.
abstract.cn: 想象一位主教与一只狐猴共用一个词，却永不相见。

abstract.en: Picture a whole order named after being first, though nobody said first in what.
abstract.cn: 想象整个目因「第一」得名，却没人说是在什么上第一。

examples.en: The primate order includes humans, which is why the name once caused offence.
examples.cn: 灵长目包含人类，这正是这个名称曾引起不快的原因。

examples.en: Primate behaviour is studied at long-term field sites more than in cages.
examples.cn: 灵长类行为更多在长期野外站点研究，而非在笼中。

examples.en: The primate of the province wore the same title as the animal on the poster.
examples.cn: 教省的首席主教与海报上那只动物带着同一个头衔。

dict_mnemonic.text: prim（第一）+ ate＝ 居首者；动物学借林奈之名指「居首的目」；记「一双朝前的眼，一只能握的手」。

root: 拉丁 primas「居首者」，来自 primus「第一」；林奈于 1758 年以 Primates 命名该目，命名动机来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one Latin word for rank: the zoological member, the laboratory subject, the ecological species, the everyday cousin, the bishop, the attributive label, the order itself, the popular catch-all and the evolutionary grade.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着一个表示位次的拉丁词展开：动物学成员、实验对象、生态物种、口语近亲、主教、定语标签、目本身、通俗统称，以及演化等级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a forward-looking eye, a hand that can grip, and a tail that can wrap a branch.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只朝前的眼、一只能抓握的手，与一条能缠住树枝的尾巴。

branches.en: RANK BECOMES A TAXON: the order and its member share one stem but not one grammar.
branches.cn: 位次变成分类：目与其成员共享词干，却不共享语法。

branches.en: THE OLDER CAREER: a bishop of the first rank entered English long before the lemurs did.
branches.cn: 更早的履历：居首的主教比狐猴更早进入英语。

branches.en: ANIMAL AS OBJECT: a laboratory subject and an ecological node, two ways of counting the same creature.
branches.cn: 动物作为对象：实验对象与生态节点，是数同一类生物的两种方式。

branches.en: KINSHIP AND CATCH-ALL: the warm word for our relatives, and the broad word for any monkey.
branches.cn: 亲缘与泛称：称近亲时的暖词，与指任何猴的宽词。

branches.en: LABEL AND GRADE: an attributive marker, and a body plan named before its taxon existed.
branches.cn: 标签与等级：定语标记，以及在分类出现之前就已得名的身体方案。

intro.en: Primate is a Latin rank word that turned into a taxonomic label; its stem also builds abstract and temporal words that are easily confused with it.
intro.cn: primate 是一个拉丁位次词，后来变成分类标签；同一词干还构成易与它混淆的抽象词与时间词。

latinIntro.en: Latin primus 'first' supplies primas 'of the first rank'; English adds -ate in the noun, while the same stem with other endings gives primacy, primal and primer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 primus「第一」提供 primas「居首的」；英语在名词上加 -ate，同一词干换其他词尾则得 primacy、primal、primer。

items.example: The stem is shared by every word in this family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干被本族各词共用。

items.structure: Latin -atus, noun ending on a rank word
items.example: The ending turns the rank word into a person or a thing.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾把位次词变成人或物。

items.meaning: a chief bishop; a member of the first order
items.example: The noun carries both careers in one spelling.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词用一种拼写承载两段履历。

items.meaning: the order of the first ones
items.example: The capitalized plural is a taxon, not a plural of the animal.
items.exampleCN: 首字母大写的复数是分类单元，不是动物的复数。

items.example: The suffix marks a discipline, not a rank.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾标记学科，而非层级。

items.example: The agent ending marks the person.
items.exampleCN: 施动词尾标记人。

items.example: The abstract noun names a position, not an animal.
items.exampleCN: 抽象名词指位置，而非动物。

items.example: The adjective moved from rank to time.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词从位次转到时间。

items.example: The word names what comes first in learning.
items.exampleCN: 这个词指学习中先来的东西。

items.example: The adjective belongs to the church sense only.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词只属教会义。

latinEntries.meaning: one of the first rank; chief

definition_zh: 灵长类学；以灵长类为对象的动物学分支
definition_en: the branch of zoology that studies primates, their behaviour, ecology and evolution
core_image: 野外营地的木板上写满同一群猴子的名字与出生年份，粉笔字换了一代又一代
scene: 野外营地的木板上写着同一群猴子的名字与出生年份，粉笔换了一代又一代。Primatology began with skins and skeletons and became a science of named individuals.
sceneCN: 这里「灵长类学」指以灵长类为对象的动物学分支（第 1 个义项：作为学科整体）；句意为灵长类学从皮毛与骨骼起家，后来变成一门研究有名有姓个体的学问。

pos.zh: 灵长类学（学科名，通常不可数）

derivatives.zh: primatology + -ist（从事者）→ 灵长类学家
primatology + -ical（关系形容词后缀）→ 灵长类学的
拉丁 primas「居首者」→ 灵长类；首席主教
希腊 ethos「习性」+ -logia「学问」→ 动物行为学（语义偏移：以行为而非分类类群为界）
希腊 anthrōpos「人」+ -logia → 人类学（语义偏移：以人为对象，与灵长类学部分交叠）

senses.title: The discipline as a whole
senses.titleCN: 作为学科整体：研究灵长类的动物学分支
senses.definition: the branch of zoology devoted to the study of primates
senses.definitionCN: 以灵长类为研究对象的动物学分支
senses.example: Primatology began with skins and skeletons and became a science of named individuals.
senses.exampleCN: 灵长类学从皮毛与骨骼起家，后来变成一门研究有名有姓个体的学问。
senses.why: Primate supplies the object, -logy supplies the account; the word therefore claims a whole discipline defined by its animals rather than by its methods.
senses.whyCN: primate 提供对象，-logy 提供叙述；这个词因此自称一门以动物而非以方法界定的完整学科。

senses.title: Field study of wild groups
senses.titleCN: 野外研究：在自然栖息地长期观察群体
senses.definition: the study of wild populations in their own habitats over long periods
senses.definitionCN: 在自然栖息地长期观察野生群体
senses.example: Field primatology depends on knowing every adult in the group by sight.
senses.exampleCN: 野外灵长类学靠的是凭肉眼就能认出群中每一只成年个体。
senses.why: A discipline defined by its animals can be practised wherever they live; the forest camp became its laboratory, and that setting produced its own standards.
senses.whyCN: 以动物界定的学科可以在动物所在之处实践；森林营地成了它的实验室，那套环境也造出了自己的标准。

senses.title: Laboratory study of cognition
senses.titleCN: 实验室认知研究：学习、记忆与解决问题
senses.definition: experimental work on learning, memory and problem solving in captive primates
senses.definitionCN: 对圈养灵长类的学习、记忆与问题解决所做的实验
senses.example: Primatology in the psychology department meant touchscreen tasks, not binoculars.
senses.exampleCN: 心理学系里的灵长类学指的是触摸屏任务，而不是望远镜。
senses.why: The same animal can be studied as a mind rather than as a population; laboratories added controlled tasks and a different vocabulary.
senses.whyCN: 同一种动物可以作为心智、而非种群来研究；实验室添进了受控任务和另一套词汇。

senses.title: Anatomy and evolutionary history
senses.titleCN: 解剖与演化史：骨骼、运动与系统发育
senses.definition: the anatomical and phylogenetic side of the field, from skeletons to locomotion
senses.definitionCN: 从骨骼到运动方式的解剖与系统发育研究
senses.example: Primatology inherited its measuring instruments from nineteenth-century anatomy.
senses.exampleCN: 灵长类学从 19 世纪的解剖学继承了测量工具。
senses.why: Before behaviour had its own methods, the only way to classify a primate was to measure it; that anatomical core never disappeared, it became the evolutionary half of the field.
senses.whyCN: 在行为研究有自身方法之前，分类灵长类的唯一办法就是测量；那个解剖内核从未消失，它成了这门学科的演化一半。

senses.title: Conservation practice
senses.titleCN: 保护实践：种群监测与栖息地保护
senses.definition: the use of the field's methods to monitor and protect threatened populations
senses.definitionCN: 用本学科方法监测与保护受威胁的种群
senses.example: Primatology now trains rangers as often as it trains students.
senses.exampleCN: 灵长类学如今培训护林员的次数不亚于培训学生。
senses.why: Because the animals studied are often endangered, the discipline's skills were recruited for protection; conservation became a working branch rather than an appendix.
senses.whyCN: 由于所研究的动物常属濒危，这门学科的技术被用于保护；保护因此成了一个实做分支，而不是附录。

senses.title: Interdisciplinary overlap
senses.titleCN: 交叉地带：与人类学、心理学的共同问题
senses.definition: the overlap with anthropology and psychology over social learning and cognition
senses.definitionCN: 与社会学习、认知问题相关、与人类学和心理学交叠的部分
senses.example: Primatology and anthropology share a seminar and argue about who owns tool use.
senses.exampleCN: 灵长类学与人类学共用一门研讨课，并为「工具使用归谁」争论。
senses.why: Primates are close relatives and also minds; the field therefore sits between zoology, psychology and anthropology, borrowing questions from each.
senses.whyCN: 灵长类既是近亲也是心智；这门学科因此位于动物学、心理学与人类学之间，向各方借问题。

senses.title: Long-term individual-based methods
senses.titleCN: 长期个体跟踪方法：认个体、记家谱、算存活
senses.definition: the method of recognising individuals and following their lives over decades
senses.definitionCN: 辨认个体、记录家谱并跨越数十年追踪其生命的方法
senses.example: Primatology changed when researchers started naming monkeys and following their children.
senses.exampleCN: 当研究者开始给猴子取名并追踪它们的后代，灵长类学就变了。
senses.why: Population averages hide what matters in a primate troop; individual recognition turns a census into a genealogy, and that method is now the discipline's signature.
senses.whyCN: 种群平均会掩盖灵长类群体里真正要紧的事；识别个体把普查变成家谱，而这一方法如今是这门学科的标志。

senses.title: Public teaching and communication
senses.titleCN: 公共教学与传播：纪录片、动物园与课程
senses.definition: the public-facing side of the field in films, zoos and classrooms
senses.definitionCN: 在影片、动物园与课堂上面对公众的一面
senses.example: Primatology supplies the stories that make people care about a forest they will never visit.
senses.exampleCN: 灵长类学提供那些让人关心一片永远不会去的森林的故事。
senses.why: A field about charismatic animals attracts audiences; the discipline therefore acquired a public voice that laboratory sciences rarely have.
senses.whyCN: 研究有魅力的动物会吸引观众；这门学科因此获得了一个实验室科学少有的大众声音。

intro.en: Primatology is a modern compound of a Latin rank word and a Greek suffix for study; the date of the coinage is only approximately known, which is the one soft point in its history.
intro.cn: primatology 是拉丁位次词与希腊「学问」后缀的现代复合词；其造词年代只有约数，这是它历史里唯一的软处。

items.en: Primas, primatis meant 'of the first rank', from primus 'first'; it named leading men and later leading bishops, and Linnaeus used the same stem for the mammalian order.
items.cn: primas, primatis 意为「居首的」，来自 primus「第一」；它先指显要人物，后指首席主教，林奈又用同一词干命名那个哺乳动物目。

items.en: -Logia 'account, study' comes from logos 'word, reason' and legein 'to gather, say'; the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
items.cn: -logia「叙述、学问」出自 logos「言词、理性」与 legein「收集、说出」；更深的印欧词根为重构。

items.en: Naturalists described and measured primates for a century before there was a named discipline; their work belonged to zoology and comparative anatomy.
items.cn: 在有了命名学科之前，博物学者已用一百年描述与测量灵长类；他们的工作属于动物学与比较解剖学。

items.en: The English word primatology is recorded only from the mid-twentieth century, when primate behaviour became a subject with its own journals.
items.cn: 英语 primatology 只见于 20 世纪中期以后的书证，当时灵长类行为成了有自身期刊的题目。

items.en: Long-term study sites and individual recognition, from the 1960s onward, gave the discipline its characteristic method and its public reputation.
items.cn: 自 20 世纪 60 年代起，长期研究站点与个体识别给了这门学科特有的方法与公众声名。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English citation is not fixed to a single year, and Linnaeus's motive for the order name Primates is inferred rather than documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语最早书证无法定到某一年；林奈以 Primates 命名该目的动机属推断，并无文献说明。

note.en: Group one holds the same-stem words that are mistaken for the discipline; group two holds neighbouring fields that study behaviour or people.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干、常被误当作本学科的词；第二组是研究行为或人的邻近领域。

entries.definition: A practitioner of the field; the discipline is the body of work, not the worker.
entries.definitionCN: 该学科的从业者；学科是工作总体，不是工作者。

entries.definition: A member of the order being studied; the animal is not the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 被研究的那个目的成员；动物不等于学科。

entries.definition: The capitalized plural names the order itself, the field's whole subject matter.
entries.definitionCN: 首字母大写的复数是目名，即本学科的全部对象。

entries.definition: Describes work or a question belonging to the field, not the field itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述属于该领域的工作或问题，而非领域本身。

entries.definition: The study of animal behaviour as such, defined by behaviour rather than by a taxonomic group.
entries.definitionCN: 以行为而非分类类群界定的动物行为研究。

entries.definition: The general study of animals, of which primatology is one branch.
entries.definitionCN: 对动物的总体研究，灵长类学只是其中一支。

entries.definition: The study of human societies and biology; it shares questions about tool use and social learning.
entries.definitionCN: 研究人类社会与生物学；在工具使用与社会学习上与本领域共享问题。

entries.definition: The study of behaviour as an adaptation to environment, applied across many animals.
entries.definitionCN: 把行为视为对环境的适应，横跨许多动物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real method names and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实方法名与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: primate 'first-rank animal' + -logy 'study' gives the study of that order, not of rank itself.
normal.cn: primate「居首的动物」+ -logy「学问」得出对那个目的研究，而非对位次的研究。

normal.en: The signature method is individual recognition: name the monkey, then follow its children.
normal.cn: 标志性方法是识别个体：先给猴子取名，再追踪它的后代。

normal.en: The family runs primate, Primates, primatology, primatologist, primatological, ethology.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 primate、Primates、primatology、primatologist、primatological、ethology。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: field primatology, comparative primatology, primatology and conservation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：野外灵长类学、比较灵长类学、灵长类学与保护。

normal.en: The field has three homes: forest camp, laboratory, and museum drawer.
normal.cn: 这个领域有三个家：森林营地、实验室与博物馆抽屉。

abstract.en: Picture a chalkboard of names that outlives the people who wrote them.
abstract.cn: 想象一块写满名字的黑板，比写它的人活得更久。

abstract.en: Picture a family album kept by a species that cannot read it.
abstract.cn: 想象一本由一个不会阅读的物种留下的家庭相册。

abstract.en: Picture a discipline that began in a drawer and ended in a forest.
abstract.cn: 想象一门从抽屉开始、在森林里落脚的科学。

examples.en: Primatology has more long-term study sites than any other branch of zoology.
examples.cn: 灵长类学的长期研究站点比动物学任何其他分支都多。

examples.en: Field primatology is limited by the patience of the animals and the funding cycle.
examples.cn: 野外灵长类学受制于动物的耐心与经费周期。

examples.en: She came to primatology from psychology and stayed for the forest.
examples.cn: 她从心理学转来灵长类学，为了森林留了下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: prim（第一）+ at（形容词）+ logy（学问）＝ 研究「居首」那个目（灵长目）的学问；记「从抽屉到森林」。

root: 拉丁 primas「居首者」（来自 primus「第一」）+ 希腊 -logia「学问、叙述」；英语 primatology 首见于 20 世纪中期，确切年代来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one discipline from its object to its public: the field, its forest camp, its laboratory, its anatomy, its conservation work, its overlap with neighbours, its signature method and its voice outside the campus.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着一门学科从对象走到公众：学科本身、森林营地、实验室、解剖、保护工作、与邻域的交叠、标志性方法，以及校园之外的声音。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a camp blackboard covered with the names and birth years of one troop, rewritten by a new generation of hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：营地木板上写满同一群猴子的名字与出生年份，又被新一代人的手重写。

branches.en: DEFINITION AND PLACE: a discipline defined by its animals, first practised where they live.
branches.cn: 定义与场所：以动物界定的学科，最先在动物所居之处实践。

branches.en: THE OTHER TWO ROOMS: controlled tasks in the lab, and the measuring of bones inherited from anatomy.
branches.cn: 另外两个房间：实验室里的受控任务，与承自解剖学的骨头测量。

branches.en: BORROWED URGENCY AND BORROWED QUESTIONS: protection as a branch, and seminars shared with anthropology.
branches.cn: 借来的紧迫与借来的问题：作为分支的保护，与和人类学共用的研讨课。

branches.en: THE SIGNATURE: recognising individuals turns a census into a genealogy.
branches.cn: 标志方法：识别个体把普查变成家谱。

branches.en: THE VOICE OUTSIDE: films and zoos make a forest matter to people who never go there.
branches.cn: 外面的声音：影片与动物园让一片森林对不去那里的人变得要紧。

intro.en: Primatology joins a Latin stem to a Greek suffix, and the resulting word has a large and confusing family of near neighbours.
intro.cn: primatology 把拉丁词干接在希腊后缀上，所得之词有一大族易混的近邻。

latinIntro.en: Latin primas supplies the first element; Greek -logia supplies the second. Latin contributes the stem only, since -logia is Greek.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 primas 提供前件；希腊 -logia 提供后件。拉丁语只提供词干，因为 -logia 是希腊语。

items.example: The stem also builds primacy and primal.
items.exampleCN: 该词干也构成 primacy 与 primal。

items.example: The noun marks a member of the first order.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词标记那个「居首」目中的成员。

items.example: Primate is the object of the study.
items.exampleCN: primate 是这门学问的对象。

items.example: The suffix also builds zoology and ethology.
items.exampleCN: 该后缀也构成 zoology 与 ethology。

items.example: The compound names the discipline in one word.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词用一个词命名该学科。

items.example: The agent ending marks the person.
items.exampleCN: 施动词尾标记人。

items.example: The adjective marks the framework.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词标记框架。

items.example: The capitalized plural is a taxon.
items.exampleCN: 首字母大写的复数是分类单元。

items.example: The neighbour field is defined by behaviour, not by group.
items.exampleCN: 邻近领域以行为界定，而非以类群。

items.example: It shares questions but not the object.
items.exampleCN: 它共享问题，但不共享对象。

definition_zh: 灵长类学家；研究灵长类行为、生态与演化的学者
definition_en: a scholar who studies primates, their behaviour, ecology and evolution
core_image: 一个人在同一棵树下坐了二十年，能叫出三代的猴子，也能背出它们的关系
scene: 同一只母猴被跟了二十年，记录者给它取了名字，也给它建了档案。The primatologist knew three generations of one family by their faces.
sceneCN: 这里指「研究灵长类的学者」（第 2 个义项：长期野外研究者）；句意为这位灵长类学家凭脸就认得一个家族的三代成员。

pos.zh: 灵长类学家（可数，复数 primatologists）

collocations.zh: 灵长类学家的田野笔记
灵长类学家与保护工作者

derivatives.zh: primatologist 的学科基座：primate + -logy → 灵长类学
primatology + -ical → 灵长类学的
拉丁 primas「居首者」→ 灵长类
etho-（希腊 ethos「习性」）+ -logist（研究者）→ 动物行为学家（语义偏移：以行为为界，不以类群为界）
zoo-（希腊 zōion「动物」）+ -logist → 动物学家（语义偏移：范围更宽）

senses.title: A practitioner of the field
senses.titleCN: 学科从业者：以灵长类学为业的人
senses.definition: a person who works professionally in primatology
senses.definitionCN: 以灵长类学为职业的人
senses.example: The primatologist knew three generations of one family by their faces.
senses.exampleCN: 这位灵长类学家凭脸就认得一个家族的三代成员。
senses.why: -ist marks the agent, so the word names whoever does what primatology describes, exactly as biologist names the doer of biology.
senses.whyCN: -ist 标记施动者，因此这个词指做灵长类学所述之事的人，正如 biologist 指做 biology 的人。

senses.title: A long-term field researcher
senses.titleCN: 长期野外研究者：在同一站点跟踪同一群体
senses.definition: one who follows the same group at one site for years or decades
senses.definitionCN: 在同一站点多年乃至数十年跟踪同一群体的人
senses.example: As a field primatologist she could tell half the troop by voice alone.
senses.exampleCN: 作为野外灵长类学家，她只听声音就能认出群中一半个体。
senses.why: The discipline's signature method is individual recognition over time, and the person who holds that method is named by the same title.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科的标志方法是跨越时间的个体识别，而掌握该方法的人就以同一头衔称呼。

senses.title: A laboratory experimentalist
senses.titleCN: 实验室研究者：做认知与比较实验
senses.definition: one who runs controlled experiments on captive primates
senses.definitionCN: 对圈养灵长类做受控实验的人
senses.example: The primatologist in the psychology building never set foot in a forest.
senses.exampleCN: 心理学楼里的这位灵长类学家从未进过森林。
senses.why: The same animal can be studied as a mind, and laboratories produced a second kind of practitioner with different training and different arguments.
senses.whyCN: 同一种动物可作为心智来研究，实验室因此造出第二类从业者，其训练与争论方式都不同。

senses.title: A conservation advocate
senses.titleCN: 保护倡导者：把研究用于种群存续
senses.definition: one who applies the field's data to protecting threatened populations
senses.definitionCN: 把研究数据用于保护受威胁种群的人
senses.example: The primatologist testified that the road would split one population in two.
senses.exampleCN: 这位灵长类学家作证说，那条路会把一个种群切成两半。
senses.why: Because the subjects are often endangered, the researcher's knowledge becomes evidence in land-use decisions; advocacy is a role the title now covers.
senses.whyCN: 由于研究对象常属濒危，研究者的知识成了土地利用决策中的证据；倡导是该头衔如今覆盖的一个角色。

senses.title: A teacher and supervisor
senses.titleCN: 教师与导师：培养学生、主持研讨
senses.definition: one employed to teach the subject and supervise research students
senses.definitionCN: 受雇教授该学科并指导研究学生的人
senses.example: The primatologist taught one course and supervised four dissertations.
senses.exampleCN: 这位灵长类学家教一门课，指导四篇学位论文。
senses.why: Once the field entered universities, the practitioner acquired the duties of a salaried academic, which the fieldworker's title did not previously imply.
senses.whyCN: 学科进入大学之后，从业者获得领薪学术人员的职责，而田野工作者的头衔此前并不含这些。

senses.title: An author of monographs
senses.titleCN: 专著作者：把长期观察写成书
senses.definition: the writer of a book-length account of one group or site
senses.definitionCN: 把对一个群体或站点的长期观察写成整本书的人
senses.example: The primatologist took eleven years to publish the monograph on the troop.
senses.exampleCN: 这位灵长类学家花了十一年才出版关于这个猴群的专著。
senses.why: Long-term data only become knowledge when written up, and the discipline's classic products are single-site books, so authorship is built into the role.
senses.whyCN: 长期数据只有写成文字才成为知识，而本学科的经典成品是单站点著作，因此著述已写进这个角色里。

senses.title: A consultant for zoos and agencies
senses.titleCN: 顾问：为动物园与管理部门提供判断
senses.definition: one who advises zoos, parks or agencies on primate care and policy
senses.definitionCN: 就灵长类饲养与管理政策向动物园、公园或部门提供意见的人
senses.example: The zoo hired a primatologist to redesign the enclosure around social groups.
senses.exampleCN: 动物园请了一位灵长类学家，按社会群体重新设计展区。
senses.why: Captive primates live in institutions, and institutions need expert judgment about grouping and enrichment; the title travels into practical settings.
senses.whyCN: 圈养灵长类生活在机构里，机构在分组与丰容上需要专家判断；这个头衔于是走进实务场景。

senses.title: A public communicator
senses.titleCN: 公共传播者：向大众讲述研究
senses.definition: one who explains primate research to the public through film, radio or writing
senses.definitionCN: 通过影片、广播或写作向大众解释灵长类研究的人
senses.example: The primatologist's radio series made a remote forest familiar to millions.
senses.exampleCN: 这位灵长类学家的广播系列让一片遥远森林为千百万人所熟悉。
senses.why: A field about charismatic animals produces public figures as well as papers, and the same title covers the person in front of a camera.
senses.whyCN: 研究有魅力动物的领域既产出论文，也产出公众人物，同一个头衔也覆盖镜头前的那个人。

intro.en: Primatologist is the field name plus the Greek agent ending, filtered through Latin and French; the only unsettled part is when the field name itself was coined.
intro.cn: primatologist 是学科名加希腊施动词尾，经拉丁语与法语过滤而成；唯一未定的部分是学科名本身何时造出。

items.en: Primas 'of the first rank' comes from primus 'first' and named leading men and later leading bishops; the zoological use of the stem dates from Linnaeus's order name.
items.cn: primas「居首的」出自 primus「第一」，先指显要人物，后指首席主教；该词干在动物学中的使用始于林奈的目名。

items.en: -Logia 'account, study' derives from logos 'word, reason' and legein 'to gather, say'; the deeper root is reconstructed.
items.cn: -logia「叙述、学问」出自 logos「言词、理性」与 legein「收集、说出」；更深词根为重构。

items.en: The agent ending reached English through Latin -ista and French -iste, from Greek -istes, and marks the person devoted to the stem's activity.
items.cn: 该施动词尾经拉丁 -ista、法语 -iste，源自希腊 -istes 进入英语，标记专注于词干所述活动的人。

items.en: Primatology is recorded from the mid-twentieth century, and primatologist followed once the field had journals and posts.
items.cn: primatology 的书证起于 20 世纪中期；待该领域有了期刊与职位，primatologist 随即出现。

items.en: Long-term field stations and university chairs turned a research topic into a career with its own training path.
items.cn: 长期野外站与大学教席把一个研究题目变成有自身训练路径的职业。

items.en: Source uncertain: no single first citation is agreed for either word, and Linnaeus's motive for Primates is inferred, not documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定：两个词都没有公认的最早书证；林奈以 Primates 命名的动机属推断，并无文献说明。

note.en: Group one holds the same-stem words most often swapped for the person; group two holds neighbouring specialists.
note.cn: 第一组是最常与人称互换的同词干词；第二组是相邻的专门研究者。

entries.definition: The discipline itself; the person is named by adding the agent ending.
entries.definitionCN: 学科本身；指人须加施动词尾。

entries.definition: A member of the order under study; it is the object, never the researcher.
entries.definitionCN: 被研究的那个目的成员；是对象，绝不是研究者。

entries.definition: The capitalized plural names the order, not a group of people.
entries.definitionCN: 首字母大写的复数命名目，不是一群人。

entries.definition: Describes work belonging to the field; it cannot stand for the worker.
entries.definitionCN: 描述属于该领域的工作，不能指工作者。

entries.definition: A specialist in animal behaviour as such, not in one taxonomic group.
entries.definitionCN: 专门研究动物行为本身，而非某一分类类群。

entries.definition: A specialist in animals generally; primatologists are zoologists with a narrow object.
entries.definitionCN: 泛研究动物的专家；灵长类学家是对象较窄的动物学家。

entries.definition: A specialist in human societies and biology; the neighbour who shares questions about tool use.
entries.definitionCN: 研究人类社会与生物学的专家；在工具使用问题上共享疑问的邻居。

entries.definition: One who works to protect species and habitats, often without research training in the group.
entries.definitionCN: 致力于保护物种与栖息地的人，常无该类群的研究训练。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real roles and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实角色与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: -ist marks the person, exactly as in biologist and zoologist.
normal.cn: -ist 标记人，与 biologist、zoologist 完全同理。

normal.en: The person is named after the method: someone who can recognise every individual in a troop.
normal.cn: 此人以方法得名：能认出群中每一只个体的人。

normal.en: The family runs primatology, primatologist, primatological, primate, Primates, ethologist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 primatology、primatologist、primatological、primate、Primates、ethologist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: a field primatologist, a primatologist's field notes, a team of primatologists.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：野外灵长类学家、灵长类学家的田野笔记、灵长类学家团队。

normal.en: The title travels: forest, laboratory, zoo, courtroom, radio studio.
normal.cn: 这个头衔会走动：森林、实验室、动物园、法庭、广播间。

abstract.en: Picture a person who knows a family's faces better than her own relatives' faces.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人对猴子家族的脸比对自家亲戚的脸更熟。

abstract.en: Picture a notebook in which the same individual appears at three different ages.
abstract.cn: 想象一本笔记，同一只个体以三个年龄出现。

abstract.en: Picture a scientist translating a forest into a sentence a city can hear.
abstract.cn: 想象一位科学家把森林翻译成城市听得懂的一句话。

examples.en: The primatologist argued that the group had been observed long enough to count as a genealogy.
examples.cn: 这位灵长类学家主张，这个群体已被观察得足够久，可以当作一份家谱。

examples.en: A primatologist was called in when the sanctuary could not stop the fights.
examples.cn: 收容所止不住打斗时，请来了一位灵长类学家。

examples.en: Primatologists disagree about how much of primate behaviour can be generalised to people.
examples.cn: 灵长类学家对灵长类行为有多少可推及人类存在分歧。

dict_mnemonic.text: prim（第一）+ at（形容词）+ logist（研究者）＝ 研究灵长目的学者；记「同一棵树下坐二十年」。

root: 拉丁 primas「居首者」（来自 primus「第一」）+ 希腊 -logia「学问」+ 希腊 -istēs（经拉丁 -ista、法语 -iste）施动词尾；确切首见年代来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one person through the places the title reaches: the practitioner, the field researcher, the laboratory experimenter, the advocate, the teacher, the author, the consultant and the public voice.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一个人走过这个头衔能到的地方：从业者、野外研究者、实验室研究者、倡导者、教师、著者、顾问与公共声音。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person who has sat under the same tree for twenty years and can name three generations of monkeys.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人在同一棵树下坐了二十年，能叫出三代猴子的名字。

branches.en: PERSON AND METHOD: the title names whoever does the field's work, and the work is long-term recognition.
branches.cn: 人与方法：头衔指做这门学问之事的人，而那件事是长期识别。

branches.en: THE SECOND ROOM: controlled experiments create a different kind of practitioner.
branches.cn: 第二个房间：受控实验造出另一类从业者。

branches.en: OUTSIDE THE CAMPUS: testimony about a road, and advice on an enclosure.
branches.cn: 校园之外：就一条路作证，就一处展区给建议。

branches.en: TEACHING AND WRITING: students supervised, and the single-site book that takes a decade.
branches.cn: 教学与写作：被指导的学生，与耗时十年的单站点著作。

branches.en: THE VOICE: the same title covers the person in front of a camera.
branches.cn: 声音：同一个头衔也覆盖镜头前的人。

intro.en: The noun is the field name plus a Greek agent ending, and nearly every near neighbour differs only by its suffix.
intro.cn: 这个名词是学科名加希腊施动词尾，几乎每个近邻词都只差一个后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin primas supplies the stem; Greek -logia and -istes supply the rest, with Latin -ista and French -iste as intermediaries. Latin contributes no additional root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 primas 提供词干；希腊 -logia 与 -istes 提供其余部分，拉丁 -ista 与法语 -iste 为中介。拉丁语不提供额外词根。

items.example: The stem builds primate and primacy alike.
items.exampleCN: 该词干同样构成 primate 与 primacy。

items.example: Primate is the object of the practitioner's work.
items.exampleCN: primate 是从业者的研究对象。

items.example: The suffix names the discipline.
items.exampleCN: 该后缀命名学科。

items.example: The ending separates the person from the field.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾把人从学科中分出。

items.example: The discipline supplies the title's base.
items.exampleCN: 学科提供头衔的基座。

items.example: The word names a career and a role.
items.exampleCN: 这个词命名一种职业与角色。

items.example: The adjective marks the work, not the worker.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词标记工作，而非工作者。

items.example: The neighbour is defined by behaviour rather than group.
items.exampleCN: 邻居以行为而非类群界定。

items.example: The suffix marks an aim, not a discipline.
items.exampleCN: 该后缀标记目的，而非学科。

definition_zh: 人科演化；人科（含大猿与人类）这一支的演化史
definition_en: the evolutionary history of the family Hominidae, the great apes and humans
core_image: 一张树状图上，人类那一支被画在猿类中间，不在树顶
scene: 展厅的树状图上，人类那一支被画在猿类中间，而不是树顶。Hominid evolution looks less like a march to the top than like a family album with missing pages.
sceneCN: 这里「人科演化」指人科这一支的演化史（第 1 个义项：科级演化史）；句意为这里的人科演化与其说像向顶端进军，不如说像一本缺页的家庭相册。

pos.zh: 人科演化（不可数；旧义仅指人类这一支的演化）

collocations.phrase: the fossil record of hominid evolution

derivatives.zh: 拉丁 homo（人）+ -idae（科级词尾）→ 人科成员：演化叙述中的主体
拉丁 evolutio「展开」→ 演化（语义偏移：从书卷展开到形态逐代展开）
evolution + -ary → 演化的
拉丁 homo + -idae → 人科（科名，含大猿与人类）
paleo-（希腊「古老」）+ anthropology → 古人类学（语义偏移：以化石重建这段演化）
拉丁 homo + -ini（族级词尾）→ 人族成员（语义偏移：层级收窄到人类这一支）

senses.title: The family-level history
senses.titleCN: 科级演化史：含大猿与人类的整段历史
senses.definition: the evolutionary history of the family Hominidae as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体的人科（含大猿与人类）的演化史
senses.example: Hominid evolution looks less like a march to the top than like a family album with missing pages.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的人科演化与其说像向顶端进军，不如说像一本缺页的家庭相册。
senses.why: Hominidae marks the family and evolutio marks the unrolling, so the phrase covers every branch of that family, not only the human one.
senses.whyCN: Hominidae 标记科，evolutio 标记展开，因此这个短语覆盖该科的每一支，而不只人类这一支。

senses.title: The traditional narrow sense
senses.titleCN: 旧日窄义：仅指人类这一支的演化
senses.definition: in older writing, the evolution of the human line only
senses.definitionCN: 旧文献中仅指人类这一支的演化
senses.example: Older textbooks titled hominid evolution and meant only the ancestors of people.
senses.exampleCN: 旧教科书题为「人科演化」，实际只指人类的祖先。
senses.why: Because hominid once excluded the other apes, the phrase inherited that restriction; the same title now covers much more than its first readers expected.
senses.whyCN: 由于 hominid 曾排除其他猿类，这个短语继承了那一限制；同样的标题如今覆盖的范围远超最初读者的预想。

senses.title: The fossil sequence
senses.titleCN: 化石序列：可被排列的那串证据
senses.definition: the ordered series of fossils from which the history is reconstructed
senses.definitionCN: 据以重建这段历史的化石序列
senses.example: The fossil record of hominid evolution is thickest where sediments are volcanic.
senses.exampleCN: 火山沉积所在之处，人科演化的化石记录最厚。
senses.why: A history is invisible; a sequence of dated specimens is readable. The phrase shifts to the evidence whenever a claim must be checked against what has been found.
senses.whyCN: 历史看不见，定过年的标本序列却可读。每当主张需要对照实物检验，这个短语就转向证据。

senses.title: Anatomical transitions
senses.titleCN: 解剖转变：骨盆、牙齿与颅骨的变化
senses.definition: the anatomical changes, such as bipedalism, tooth reduction and brain expansion
senses.definitionCN: 骨盆、牙齿与颅骨等方面的解剖变化，如两足行走、牙齿缩小与脑扩大
senses.example: Hominid evolution is read from a pelvis before it is read from a skull.
senses.exampleCN: 人科演化先从骨盆读出，然后才从颅骨读出。
senses.why: Bones are the only direct evidence of ancient bodies, so the phrase's core chapters are anatomical; each transition is a change in a named structure.
senses.whyCN: 骨骼是古代身体唯一的直接证据，因此这个短语的核心章节是解剖的；每一次转变都是某一具名结构的变化。

senses.title: Adaptive and behavioural change
senses.titleCN: 适应与行为变化：食性、社会与工具
senses.definition: shifts in diet, social organisation and tool use treated as adaptations
senses.definitionCN: 把食性、社会组织与工具使用视为适应的变化
senses.example: Hominid evolution includes a diet that moved from leaves to roots and meat.
senses.exampleCN: 人科演化包括食性从叶子转向根茎与肉。
senses.why: Evolution selects on behaviour as well as bone, and behaviour can be inferred from teeth, campsites and stone; this chapter therefore mixes anatomy with inference.
senses.whyCN: 演化既选择骨骼，也选择行为，而行为可从牙齿、营地与石器推断；因此这一章把解剖与推断混在一起。

senses.title: The effect of taxonomic revision
senses.titleCN: 分类修订的影响：名词改变如何改写故事
senses.definition: the way reclassification changes what the history is said to contain
senses.definitionCN: 重新分类如何改变这段历史的内容
senses.example: Hominid evolution expanded as a category the moment the great apes were admitted to the family.
senses.exampleCN: 大猿一被纳入这个科，人科演化作为一个范畴也随之扩大。
senses.why: Because the phrase is built on a rank name, any change in that rank rewrites the sentence; taxonomy is not background but part of the claim.
senses.whyCN: 由于短语建立在层级名上，层级一变，句子就要重写；分类不是背景，而是主张的一部分。

senses.title: Molecular evidence
senses.titleCN: 分子证据：基因与谱系分化时间
senses.definition: the genetic evidence that dates splits and tracks gene flow
senses.definitionCN: 为分化定年并追踪基因流的遗传学证据
senses.example: Molecular work pushed the split with chimpanzees back millions of years before the fossils did.
senses.exampleCN: 分子研究把与黑猩猩的分化时间推前了数百万年，早于化石所能显示。
senses.why: DNA carries a record that bones do not, so the phrase now covers divergence dates and interbreeding as well as skeletons.
senses.whyCN: DNA 携带骨骼所没有的记录，因此这个短语如今除骨架外也覆盖分化年代与杂交。

senses.title: The teaching narrative
senses.titleCN: 教学叙事：展厅与课本讲的那一版
senses.definition: the simplified account presented in museums, courses and documentaries
senses.definitionCN: 博物馆、课程与纪录片所呈现的简化叙述
senses.example: The hominid evolution on the wall ends with a figure holding a spear and then a phone.
senses.exampleCN: 墙上的人科演化以一个先持矛、后持电话的形象收尾。
senses.why: Any long history must be edited to be taught; the public version is a genuine sense, and its simplifications are what specialists attack.
senses.whyCN: 任何漫长的历史都必须经过剪辑才能教；公共版本是一个真实义项，而它的简化正是专家攻击的地方。

intro.en: The phrase joins a nineteenth-century family name to a Latin word for unrolling; the family name has been redefined, and that redefinition is part of the phrase's history.
intro.cn: 这个短语把 19 世纪的科名接在拉丁语「展开」一词上；科名曾被重新界定，而那次重新界定也是短语历史的一部分。

items.en: The family name was formed on the Latin stem homin- with the family ending -idae, and originally held humans and their extinct relatives.
items.cn: 科名以拉丁词干 homin- 加科级词尾 -idae 构成，最初只含人类及其已灭绝亲属。

items.en: Evolvere 'to roll out, unroll', from ex- plus volvere 'to roll', supplies the image of a folded record opened in order.
items.cn: evolvere「展开、卷开」由 ex- 加 volvere「卷」构成，提供把折叠记录按序打开的意象。

items.en: Evolutio named the act of unrolling and had no biological sense in classical Latin; the modern sense is an English development.
items.cn: evolutio 指展开动作，古典拉丁语中无生物学义；现代义是英语的发展。

items.en: Comparative genetics later placed the great apes inside Hominidae, so hominid evolution came to cover apes as well as people.
items.cn: 比较遗传学后来把大猿放进 Hominidae，于是人科演化也开始覆盖猿类。

items.en: DNA evidence redated major splits and revealed interbreeding, adding chapters that the fossil record alone could not supply.
items.cn: DNA 证据为各大分化重新定年，并揭示杂交，添进了仅靠化石无法提供的章节。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact phrase has no agreed first citation, and the deeper origin of homo behind homin- remains unknown, with the humus reading a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这一确切短语没有公认的最早书证；homin- 背后的 homo 更深来源仍不明，与 humus 的读法是假说。

note.en: Group one holds the parallel phrases that differ only in their rank word; group two holds the disciplines and mechanisms that explain the history.
note.cn: 第一组是仅差层级词的平行短语；第二组是解释这段历史的学科与机制。

entries.definition: The history of the human line after the split; narrower than the family-level phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 分化之后人类这一支的历史；比科级短语窄。

entries.definition: The history of the tribe Hominini, which excludes the other great apes.
entries.definitionCN: 人族的历史，不含其他大猿。

entries.definition: A member of the family; the phrase names the history those members produced.
entries.definitionCN: 该科的一个成员；短语命名这些成员所造成的历史。

entries.definition: The capitalized family name, a category rather than a process.
entries.definitionCN: 首字母大写的科名，是范畴而非过程。

entries.definition: The field that reconstructs this history from fossils and archaeology.
entries.definitionCN: 靠化石与考古重建这段历史的学科。

entries.definition: The broad science of descent and selection, of which this history is one case.
entries.definitionCN: 研究谱系与选择的宽泛科学，这段历史只是其中一例。

entries.definition: The differential survival of variants; it explains but does not name the history.
entries.definitionCN: 变体的差异化存活；它作解释，但不命名这段历史。

entries.definition: The surviving remains taken as a body of evidence, not the interpretation built on them.
entries.definitionCN: 留存遗存作为证据总体，而非据其建立的解释。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real ranks, real chapters and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实层级、真实章节与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Hominidae is the family, evolutio is the unrolling: the phrase unrolls a whole family, not just our branch.
normal.cn: Hominidae 是科，evolutio 是展开：短语展开的是整个科，不只是我们这一支。

normal.en: The chapters are gait, teeth, brain, diet, tools, dispersal, genes, and the museum version.
normal.cn: 各章是步态、牙齿、脑、食性、工具、扩散、基因，以及展厅版本。

normal.en: The family runs Hominidae, hominid, hominin, human, evolution, evolutionary, paleoanthropology.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 Hominidae、hominid、hominin、human、evolution、evolutionary、paleoanthropology。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: the fossil record of hominid evolution, hominid evolution in Africa.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：人科演化的化石记录、非洲的人科演化。

normal.en: Taxonomy is part of the claim: widen the family and the sentence widens with it.
normal.cn: 分类本身是主张的一部分：科一变宽，句子也跟着变宽。

abstract.en: Picture a family album whose missing pages are the ones everyone asks about.
abstract.cn: 想象一本家庭相册，缺的正是人人追问的那几页。

abstract.en: Picture a tree drawn on a wall, with our branch placed among the others rather than above them.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上画着一棵树，我们那一支被放在其他支之间，而不是其上。

abstract.en: Picture a label change that silently rewrites a museum's whole first room.
abstract.cn: 想象一次标签改动，悄悄改写了博物馆整个第一展厅。

examples.en: Hominid evolution is dated by volcanic layers more reliably than by tooth size.
examples.cn: 给人科演化定年，靠火山层比靠牙齿大小更可靠。

examples.en: The exhibition revised its hominid evolution chart after the new jaw was described.
examples.cn: 新下颌被描述之后，展览修改了它的人科演化图。

examples.en: Students often arrive believing hominid evolution is a single line upward.
examples.cn: 学生常带着「人科演化是一条向上的直线」这一想法来上课。

dict_mnemonic.text: hominid（人科的）+ evolution（展开）＝ 人科这一支的展开；记「人类那一支画在猿类中间，不在树顶」。

root: 新拉丁 Hominidae（拉丁 homo「人」+ -idae 科级词尾）+ 拉丁 evolutio「展开」，来自 evolvere（ex- + volvere「卷」）；homo 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses unroll one family history: the whole family, the older narrow reading, the fossil sequence, the anatomical transitions, behaviour, the effect of reclassification, the molecular chapters and the museum version.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项展开一段科级历史：整个科、旧日窄义、化石序列、解剖转变、行为、重新分类的影响、分子章节，以及展厅版本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tree diagram on a museum wall with the human branch drawn among the apes, not at the top.
core.cn: 核心意象：博物馆墙上的树状图，人类那一支画在猿类之间，不在顶端。

branches.en: TWO SCOPES OF ONE TITLE: the whole family now, and the human line only in older texts.
branches.cn: 同一个标题的两种范围：如今的整个科，与旧文本里仅人类一支。

branches.en: READING THE BODY: a dated sequence of fossils, then pelvis, teeth and skull.
branches.cn: 读身体：先是定年的化石序列，再是骨盆、牙齿与颅骨。

branches.en: WHAT BONES ONLY SUGGEST: diet, society and tools inferred from teeth and campsites.
branches.cn: 骨头只能暗示的东西：由牙齿与营地推断食性、社会与工具。

branches.en: WHEN THE FRAME MOVES: reclassification widens the sentence, and DNA adds dates bones cannot give.
branches.cn: 框架移动时：重新分类拓宽句子，DNA 添进骨头给不出的年代。

branches.en: THE EDITED VERSION: the wall chart that ends with a figure holding a phone.
branches.cn: 剪辑版：以持电话的形象收尾的墙上图表。

intro.en: Both elements are borrowed, but the family name is a taxonomic formation and the second word is a Latin verb family, so each half can be read separately.
intro.cn: 两个成分都是借来的，但科名是分类学构造，第二个词是拉丁动词词族，因此两半可分别读出。

latinIntro.en: New Latin Hominidae supplies the first element; Latin evolvere and evolutio supply the second. The Greek-derived -idae is a taxonomic ending rather than a Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 新拉丁 Hominidae 提供前件；拉丁 evolvere 与 evolutio 提供后件。源自希腊的 -idae 是分类词尾，而非拉丁词根。

items.example: The stem appears in every rank name of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干出现在该族的每个层级名中。

items.structure: New Latin family ending from Greek -idai
items.example: The ending marks the rank that the phrase's history covers.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾标记这段历史所覆盖的层级。

items.example: The noun names the actors in the history.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名历史中的行动者。

items.example: The prefix gives the direction of unrolling.
items.exampleCN: 前缀给出展开的方向。

items.example: The root supplies the image behind the second word.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供第二个词背后的意象。

items.example: The noun carries the scroll image into biology.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词把书卷意象带进生物学。

items.example: The adjective marks the framework of the claim.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词标记主张的框架。

items.example: The compound names the field that reads the record.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词命名读记录的那门学科。

items.example: The narrower word marks the human branch within the family.
items.exampleCN: 较窄的这个词标记科内的人类一支。

latinEntries.structure: Hominidae (New Latin, f. plural, family rank)
latinEntries.meaning: the family of humans and great apes
